  • 23. Animal Restaurant
  • 24. Slide The Shakes
  • 25. Find My Friends
  • 26. Bumped Out

26+ Best Snapchat Games You Have to Play

From interactive games to adventure mysteries, we have created a list that will not disappoint you.

1. Subway Surfers Airtime

A modern twist on a mobile classic, Subway Surfers Airtime brings the energy of endless running straight into Snapchat. You and your friends can play together in real time, racing to see who stays on track the longest. It captures the same colorful charm and thrill of the original while adding a fun multiplayer twist that keeps the nostalgia alive.

2. Chess Quest

For players who prefer strategy over speed, Chess Quest brings the timeless board game to Snapchat. It offers different modes like ranked battles and master challenges, making it suitable for both casual and competitive players. You can even chat with friends via text or voice while playing, so it feels more like a live match than a digital game. It’s classic chess, just more social.

3. Zombie Rescue Squad

If you enjoy a good survival challenge, Zombie Rescue Squad throws you right into a city overrun by the undead. Your mission is to save survivors while dodging and taking down zombies. The game auto-fires for you, so the focus is on moving smartly, collecting weapons, and managing health packs. Stay close to survivors for bonus points and that extra sense of victory.

4. Cube Surfer

Cube Surfer brings a clever twist to running games. You collect yellow cubes to stack beneath your character, helping you glide over red barriers that block your path. The trick lies in grabbing enough cubes to stay safe while staying fast. It’s simple, bright, and surprisingly addictive once you find your rhythm.

5. Crazy Run

Crazy Run turns obstacle racing into pure chaos and fun. You’ll dodge hot steam, leap over walls, swing across bars, and even avoid flying sausages, all while racing against your friends’ Bitmojis. The gameplay is fast and interactive, with on-screen prompts guiding your every move. Watching your friends stumble through the same challenges makes it one of the best Snapchat games you have to play.

6. Super Snappy Bowling

When real bowling isn’t an option, this one’s the next best thing. Super Snappy Bowling recreates the arcade feel with simple touch controls, pull down to aim, swipe up to roll, and hold to guide your throw. Competing against friends makes every strike or gutter ball a little more dramatic. It’s casual, competitive, and perfect for quick matches.

7. Tiny Royale

For those who love battle royale chaos, Tiny Royale packs all the intensity into bite-sized matches. You can play solo or form a squad of up to four players, scavenging for weapons and fighting your way to the top among 30 competitors. Quick rounds, tight maps, and endless action make it one of the best Snapchat games you have to play.

8. Island Jump

Island Jump keeps your reflexes sharp with its quick-tap gameplay. You hop from one floating island to another, collecting coins while dodging sharks, eagles, and poles. The goal is to stay alive and go as far as you can without missing a step. It’s an easy game to pick up but hard to master, which makes every run addictive.

9. Bitmoji Tennis

Bitmoji Tennis is one of the best Snapchat games you have to play. Instead of worrying about perfect timing, you just move your player left and right while your Bitmoji handles the swings. Tilt your phone to aim and adjust the shot angle. You can challenge friends or play solo, with adjustable difficulty levels that keep matches interesting.

10. Ludo Club

The much-loved Indian board game makes its way to Snapchat through Ludo Club, developed in partnership with Moonfrog Labs. It brings all the nostalgic fun of rolling dice and racing tokens, only now, you can do it with friends online! The interface is clean and lively, making it easy to jump into a quick match whenever you like.

11. Let’s Go Hoops!

Basketball fans will have a blast with Let’s Go Hoops!, a competitive mini-game where you race your friends to score five baskets first. You can challenge your Snapchat pals or get matched with random players. Winning rounds earns you in-game crystals to unlock fun Bitmoji dance moves, hoops, and basketballs. It’s simple, addictive, and full of friendly rivalry, and one of the best Snapchat games you have to play.

12. Ready Set Golf

Ready Set Golf brings classic golf fun into short, competitive rounds with friends. You just pull back, aim, and release to send the ball flying toward the hole, all under a 60-second timer. Quick reflexes and precision make all the difference here. After each match, rankings appear so you can brag (or regroup) for the next round.

13. AlphaBear Hustle

If you love word games, AlphaBear Hustle is your playground. The goal is to form meaningful words from random letters, and each correct word helps you build your own quirky village filled with bears, trampolines, and pine trees. You can play solo or invite friends for a friendly word duel. It’s fun, creative, and a nice break from fast-paced action games, making it one of the best Snapchat games you have to play.

14. Om Nom Run

If endless runner games are your thing, Om Nom Run should be on your list. Much like Subway Surfers, this one keeps you hooked with its fast pace and colorful graphics. The visuals are slightly sharper, and you can use power-ups to get a strong start or dodge tricky obstacles. It’s perfect for quick gaming sessions with friends, offering both excitement and challenge in every round.

15. Flip the Egg

Simple in idea but tricky in execution, Flip the Egg will test your timing skills. You just need to tap and hold to flip the egg out of the pan. Sounds easy, right? Not quite. Getting that perfect flip takes practice and patience. Compete with your Snapchat friends and see who tops the leaderboard. It’s the kind of casual, fun game that’s harder than it looks.

16. Snake Squad

Snake Squad takes the classic “grow and survive” idea and turns it into a fun multiplayer showdown. You control a snake, collect glowing dots, and grow larger while avoiding bigger players. It starts easily but quickly turns competitive, testing your reflexes and strategy. The longer you last, the tougher and more rewarding it gets!

17. Let’s Do It!

If making decisions with friends always turns into chaos, Let’s Do It! keeps things simple and fun. This Snap Mini helps you pick what to watch, listen to, cook, or even do next, all with just a tap. It’s like a tiny suggestion engine built for group indecision. Whether you’re planning a movie night or a quick hangout, this app takes the guesswork out of it.

18. Color Galaxy

Color Galaxy turns territory control into a vibrant, fast-paced challenge. You drive around the map, claiming new zones by tracing loops and returning to your base to secure them. One wrong move, so cross your own trail or an opponent’s, and you’re out. It’s simple, colorful, and surprisingly tense, and one of the best Snapchat games you have to play.

19. Color Together

If you like to unwind with something calm, Color Together is the perfect creative break. It lets you color digital art sheets with a wide palette and relaxing background music. You can even paint alongside a friend, turning it into a shared creative session. It’s peaceful, satisfying, and a nice contrast to Snapchat’s faster-paced games.

20. Aquapark: Multiplayer Edition

Set in a colorful water park, Aquapark is all about racing to the finish line before anyone else. You can speed down slides, bump opponents off track, or risk shortcuts for faster wins. It’s lighthearted, fast-paced fun, ideal for friendly rivalries and laughter with your Snapchat crew.

21. Hex FRVR

Puzzle lovers will appreciate Hex FRVR, a relaxing yet challenging twist on Tetris. You need to fit hexagonal pieces into rows, clearing space as you go. The trick is to plan ahead before the board fills up. It’s easy to learn but surprisingly deep once you start chasing higher scores, perfect for puzzle enthusiasts who like a mental workout.

22. Let’s Do It!

If making decisions with friends always turns into chaos, Let’s Do It! keeps things simple and fun. This Snap Mini helps you pick what to watch, listen to, cook, or even do next, all with just a tap. It’s like a tiny suggestion engine built for group indecision. Whether you’re planning a movie night or a quick hangout, this is one of the best Snapchat games you have to play.

23. Animal Restaurant

In Animal Restaurant, your staff are cats and your guests are all kinds of cute animals—dogs, rabbits, badgers, and more. You earn cod, the in-game currency, to unlock new areas like a fish pond, garden, or buffet room. Each upgrade brings more customers and boosts your restaurant’s charm. You can also compare your progress on the leaderboard to see how your café stacks up against friends.

24. Slide The Shakes

Slide The Shakes is simple yet addictive. You just flick milkshakes across the table so they land perfectly in the green zone near your friend’s Bitmoji. Too soft, and you won’t make it. Too hard, and the shake goes flying off the table. The challenge ramps up each round, keeping things fresh and surprisingly tricky, making it one of the best Snapchat games you have to play.

25. Find My Friends

If you loved “Where’s Waldo?” you’ll enjoy Find My Friends. It’s a visual puzzle where you hunt for a specific Bitmoji among a crowd, matching tiny details like poses and facial expressions. Some rounds are easy wins, while others make you squint at the screen for that one perfectly hidden Bitmoji. Compete with friends on the leaderboard to claim bragging rights.

26. Bumped Out

Bumped Out takes the idea of bumper cars to the next level. You steer your tiny car using an on-screen pad and try to knock everyone else off the island. It’s easy to start but surprisingly tricky to master. Staying on the platform is tough enough, especially when your friends gang up to push you off.

Also Read: How Long Are Snapchat Video

Now that you have seen the best Snapchat games you have to play, we hope your doubts are cleared with the methods shown in this guide. Keep visiting TechCult to know the latest tech walkarounds. If you have any queries or suggestions, do reach out to us in the comment section.

content:
Although Snapchat is used for taking quick snaps, one of its most talked-about features is the best friends list. This ranking shows which friends you snap with most often and tracks your closest connections on the platform. But this also brings in lots of confusion around their workings and difficulty deciphering them. You might be curious about how the list actually works or how to see who made your top friends. Today, we will unravel this mystery!

  • How to Add Someone to Your Best Friends List on Snapchat

Snapchat Best Friends List

Now you can manage your social life on the app without creating unnecessary drama.

💕 Best Friends Forever: The double heart represents engaging with each other for two months and consistently being each other’s best friends.

❤️Super Best Friends: This indicates that you have been best friends for the past two weeks.

💛 Besties: The yellow heart represents your friendship with each other.

😊 Close Friends: Although this contact is one of your closest friends, you don’t always snap and talk with them.

😬 Common Best Friends: You and your best pal are mutual besties.

😎 Mutual BFs: One of your best friends is also one of this Snapchat user’s best friends.

How Many Best Friends Can You Have on Snapchat?

Currently, users are allowed to have up to 8 best friends simultaneously.

Who Can See Your Best Friends List?

Only you are allowed to see your best friends on Snapchat. Other users do not get emojis beside their name with you.

How to Add Someone to Your Best Friends List on Snapchat

With a few changes in your interactions, you can make any user your best friend. Follow the guide Snapchat Red Heart Emoji Meaning Explained: What Does It Mean & How to Get.

How to See Your Best Friends List on Snapchat

You can easily check out your entire friends list:

  1. Open Snapchat and tap on your profile in the top left corner.
  2. Swipe down and tap on My Friends under Friends.

You will see a hierarchical list of all best friends.

content:
With the rise of new social media platforms, people have started to bid farewell to the old ones. Unfortunately, Snapchat has seen a decline in its popularity since users have grown out of the app. If you’re one of those who are looking for how to permanently delete your Snapchat account, you’re in the right place. Let’s show you the way out!

  • How to Delete Snapchat Account Permanently
  • Method 1: Via Mobile
  • Method 2: Via Desktop
  • Why Can’t I Delete Snapchat Account?
  • Can I Recover My Deleted Snapchat Account after 30 Days?

How to Delete Snapchat Account Permanently

Let’s take a look at removing your Snapchat account from any devices.

Method 1: Via Mobile

Here’s how you so from your smartphone:

  1. Open Snapchat and tap on your profile from the top left corner.
  2. Tap on the settings icon from the top right corner.
  3. Swipe down and select Delete Account under MY ACCOUNT.
  4. Type in your username and password under Delete account.
  5. Select CONTINUE.

Your account will be deleted or deactivated.

Method 2: Via Desktop

Follow the steps to do the same from the web version:

  1. Visit the official site of Snapchat accounts portal.
  2. Type in your username and password.
  3. Select Continue.
  4. Scroll down and select Delete my account.
  5. Type in your username and password under Delete account.
  6. Select CONTINUE.

This way, your account will be deleted.

Why Can’t I Delete Snapchat Account?

If you’re having a hard time deleting your account, here are some reasons why:

  • Incorrect username or password.
  • Your account is permanently locked by Snapchat.
  • The deactivation period of 30 days has not been completed.

Can I Recover My Deleted Snapchat Account after 30 Days?

No, unfortunately, Snapchat does not allow users to recover their account after the 30 days of deactivation period.

title: What Does Green Dot Mean on Snapchat?
subtitle: What Does Green Dot Mean on Snapchat: When a user is online or has recently used Snapchat, a green dot icon appears on top of them
author: Techcult
summary: What Does Green Dot Mean on Snapchat: When a user is online or has recently used Snapchat, a green dot icon appears on top of them
content:
We’ve all been there, scrolling through Snapchat, sending streaks to friends, when suddenly you notice a tiny green dot next to someone’s name. Since the platform is designed around using snaps to have conversations in real time, having an activity status makes it easier for users to keep up with discussions. But you can’t help but wonder what does that green dot actually mean, then you’re at the right place! Let’s find out the answer.

  • What Does Green Dot Mean on Snapchat? 
  • How Long Does the Green Dot Stay on Snapchat?
  • Why Can’t I See the Green Dot on Snapchat?
  • How to Turn Off the Green Dot on Snapchat

What Does Green Dot Mean on Snapchat? 

When a user is online or has recently been actively using the platform, a green dot icon appears on top of them. Knowing when friends are available to talk or instantly view your snaps is made easier by this function.

How Long Does the Green Dot Stay on Snapchat?

The green dot can show up for two reasons:

  • It displays if a person is online right now or has been active recently. After the user exits the program, the dot remains visible for three to five minutes. A timestamp, such as 25m ago, can appear next to the dot if the person has just used Snapchat.
  • When you switch on the camera on your laptop or smartphone, it also acts as a privacy notification and lets you know.

Why Can’t I See the Green Dot on Snapchat?

You might have this feature turned off if you can’t see the activity status icon. Furthermore, the feature is not available on your primary chat threads; it is only displayed in the Add Friends list.

How to Turn Off the Green Dot on Snapchat

If you wish to protect your privacy, you can also disable the activity status on Snapchat. Here’s how:

  1. Open Snapchat and tap on your profile from the top left corner.
  2. Select the settings icon from the top right corner.
  3. Swipe down and tap on Activity indicator under PRIVACY CONTROLS.
  4. Now, turn the toggle off for Activity indicator.

This way, your friends will no longer know if you’ve been active.

Also Read: What is a Clipboard on Snapchat?

Now you will no longer have a difficult time figuring what does the green dot icon it mean on Snapchat after following this guide. For more helpful tips and tricks, stay tuned, and feel free to share your suggestions in the comments below.

title: What is a Clipboard on Snapchat?
subtitle: What is a Clipboard on Snapchat: Snapchat Clipboard is designed to hold copied text, links, or media to paste on here or other apps
author: Techcult
summary: What is a Clipboard on Snapchat: Snapchat Clipboard is designed to hold copied text, links, or media to paste on here or other apps
content:
Snapchat has evolved into more than just a place for disappearing snaps. Filters, stickers, and text tools help you express yourself, but one lesser-known but super handy tool is the Snapchat Clipboard. Whether you’re drafting a caption, reusing a witty reply, or saving something to paste into your story later, the clipboard keeps things handy. Knowing what a Clipboard is on Snapchat helps you unlock this small but mighty feature. Let’s get started!

  • What is a Clipboard on Snapchat?
  • How to Enable the Clipboard on Snapchat
  • How Does Snapchat Clipboard Work?

What is a Clipboard on Snapchat?

Snapchat Clipboard is designed to temporarily hold copied text, links, or media. It helps you quickly access content without leaving the app. Additionally, users have the option to paste this material in Snapchat or a separate app.

How to Enable the Clipboard on Snapchat

If you want to start using the clipboard, here’s how you can turn it on:

  1. Open Snapchat and tap on your profile in the top left corner.
  2. Tap on the settings icon in the top right corner.
  3. Swipe down and select Permissions under ADDITIONAL SERVICES.
  4. Now, select Tap to enable under Clipboard.

The clipboard will be turned on.

How Does Snapchat Clipboard Work?

One of Snapchat’s special features is the clipboard, which lets users record and share text, photos, and other data straight from the app. Here’s how it works:

  • Snapchat will automatically store your camera roll with the images and videos you take.
  • If you wish to share the picture or video with someone, you can hit the Share button and choose the Copy option.
  • Your clipboard will receive a copy of the picture or video. You can just copy and paste the picture or video into a different program or document.

Now that you know what a Clipboard is on Snapchat, we hope your doubts are cleared with the methods shown in this guide. Keep visiting TechCult to know the latest tech walkarounds. If you have any queries or suggestions, do reach out to us in the comment section.

title: How to Fix Snapchat Cameos Not Loading
subtitle: How to Fix Snapchat Cameos Not Loading: Long press home the button, Swipe up on Snapchat, Open app after some time
author: Techcult
summary: How to Fix Snapchat Cameos Not Loading: Long press home the button, Swipe up on Snapchat, Open app after some time
content:
Apart from the infamous Snapchat filters, Cameo is another way to add a fun, personalized twist to your selfies. But imagine trying to send a funny animation to your friends, but your cameos just won’t cooperate. You’re not alone if you’ve noticed them not loading or showing up in the chat bar. Knowing how to fix Snapchat cameos not loading can get your expressive chats back on track. Let’s get started!

  • How to Fix Snapchat Cameos Not Loading
  • Method 1: Via Remove from Background
  • Method 2: Update App
  • Method 3: Via Check Storage Space
  • Method 4: Via Clear Cache
  • Method 5: Via Uninstall and Reinstall
  • Method 5: Via Force Stop
  • Method 7: Via VPN
  • Method 8: Via Hard Reset 
  • Method 9: Via Contact Snapchat Support

How to Fix Snapchat Cameos Not Loading

Before you give up on your perfect reaction video, try out these fixes to solve your issue.

Method 1: Via Remove from Background

The quickest way to fix any glitch is by removing the actively running app from your background. Swipe on your home button and then swipe up on Snapchat. Open the app after some time to see if this fixes your problem.

Method 2: Update App

Another way is to ensure that you are running on the latest version of Snapchat. This way, any internal bugs or software glitches should be automatically fixed and you can use the app smoothly.

Method 3: Via Check Storage Space

It is important to have enough storage on your phone for Snapchat to work properly and get the latest updates. Therefore, before you try hard fixes, check for proper space available on your smartphone.

Method 4: Via Clear Cache

If you have been using the platform for a long time, it’s time to clear out some cache.

Option 1: Via Snapchat Settings

Users can directly clear out the overtime collected cache from the Snapchat app:

  1. Open Snapchat and tap on your profile at the top left corner
  2. Tap on the settings icon.
  3. Swipe down and tap on Clear data under PRIVACY CONTROLS.
  4. Then, select Clear Cache.
  5. Now, tap on Clear.
  6. Re-open Snapchat.

Now your issue should be fixed.

Option 2: Via Android

You can do the same from your device settings if you use an Android Smartphone:

Note: Not all Android devices have the same interface since they vary from manufacturer to manufacturer. Hence, ensure the correct settings have been selected according to your device’s language. 

  1. Open Settings and tap on App.
  2. Swipe down and select Snapchat.
  3. Tap on Storage.
  4. Then, select Clear Cache.
  5. Restart your phone.

Now you should be able to use the app without any trouble.

Option 3: Via iPhone

If you’re wondering why video call not showing me on Snapchat on iPhone, offload old data: Here’s how:

  1. Open Settings and tap on General.
  2. Swipe down and tap on iPhone Storage.
  3. Select Snapchat.
  4. Then, tap on Offload App.
  5. Select Offload App from the confirmation prompt.
  6. Open App Store and search for Snapchat.
  7. Tap on Get to install the app.

This way, you will be able to fix any slow processes on Snapchat.

Method 5: Via Uninstall and Reinstall

Lastly, if nothing works, then you can uninstall Instagram to get rid of any app issues. Wait for some time and reinstall to see if your problem persists.

Method 5: Via Force Stop

You can also force stop Snapchat on your Android smartphone:

  1. Open Settings and tap on App.
  2. Swipe down and select Snapchat.
  3. Tap on App info.
  4. Now, select Force stop.

The app will be closed properly.

Method 7: Via VPN

Due to geographical restrictions, not all countries have the Snapchat Cameo feature available. If you belong to any such region where this may be unavailable, then you can use a VPN to change countries.

Method 8: Via Hard Reset 

If nothing seems to be working, then you may have to reset your phone:

  1. Open Settings and tap on General.
  2. Swipe down and tap on Transfer or Reset iPhone.
  3. Now, select Reset All Settings.
  4. Enter your passcode.
  5. Restart iPhone.

This way, your apps should start working with no issues.

Method 9: Via Contact Snapchat Support

If you are out of solutions, then it may be time to get in touch with Snapchat Support. Submit your enquiry with pictures and wait to hear directly from the app experts.

title: How to Change Your Snapchat Email
subtitle: How to Change Your Snapchat Email: Tap on the Gear icon, Tap on Email, Delete your existing email address, Enter the new one, Tap on SAVE
author: Techcult
summary: How to Change Your Snapchat Email: Tap on the Gear icon, Tap on Email, Delete your existing email address, Enter the new one, Tap on SAVE
content:
Having an email address linked to your Snapchat account enables you to retrieve your account if you are locked out for any reason. If you no longer use your current email or want to switch to a different one, changing it can help you stay up-to-date on important notifications from the platform. In this article, we’ll cover how to change your Snapchat email.

  • How to Change Your Snapchat Email
  • How to Change Snapchat Email Without Logging In
  • Can I Switch Snapchat Email Back to My Old One?

How to Change Your Snapchat Email

Switching your email address on Snapchat is a simple process that just needs a few simple steps to complete. Here’s how you can change your email address:

  1. Open Snapchat and tap on the Bitmoji icon in the top left corner.
  2. Tap on the settings icon.
  3. Swipe down and select Email.
  4. Now, delete your existing email address, then enter the new one.
  5. Tap on CONTINUE.
  6. Now, navigate to the email address you just entered.
  7. Tap on the Confirm Email.

That’s it, now you have successfully altered your Snapchat email.

How to Change Snapchat Email Without Logging In

Unfortunately, currently, it is not possible to modify Snapchat email without logging in. 

Can I Switch Snapchat Email Back to My Old One?

Yes, it is possible to modify your Snapchat email back to the old one by following the same steps as shown above.

title: 5 Ways to Fix Snapchat Notifications Sound Not Working
subtitle: 5 Ways to Fix Snapchat Notifications Sound Not Working: Disable Silent Mode, Disconnect Bluetooth, Log out of Snapchat web and enable alerts
author: Techcult
summary: 5 Ways to Fix Snapchat Notifications Sound Not Working: Disable Silent Mode, Disconnect Bluetooth, Log out of Snapchat web and enable alerts
content:
Snapchat always keeps you in the loop with instant alerts on story replies, snaps, or calls. But when your notification sound suddenly stops working, you might miss important updates. But don’t let muted notifications make you the last to see a streak or miss out on conversations. Let’s see some quick ways to fix the Snapchat notifications sound not working and remove this audio hiccup!

  • 5 Ways to Fix Snapchat Notifications Sound Not Working
  • Method 1: Disable Silent Mode
  • Method 2: Disconnect Bluetooth Devices
  • Method 3: Log out of Snapchat Web
  • Method 4: Re-enable notifications
  • Method 5: Turn off DND and Focus mode

5 Ways to Fix Snapchat Notifications Sound Not Working

Whether it’s a phone settings glitch, accidental mute toggle, or outdated software causing the issue, keep reading to find your solution. Before you start, make sure Snapchat is updated to its latest version.

Method 1: Disable Silent Mode

The easiest way to resolve your problem is to check if your device is not in silent mode. Simply press the volume up key to the maximum level and enable sound again on any smartphone.

Method 2: Disconnect Bluetooth Devices

Another reason why your notification sound may not be working is if you have connected your phone to an external Bluetooth device. If it is connected to a headphone or earphone, then your main sound may be audible in these gadgets; therefore, turn off Bluetooth.

Method 3: Log out of Snapchat Web

If you are logged into Snapchat from the browser, you will not get the in-app notifications on your bar. Therefore, log in from the official app to enjoy alerts.

Method 4: Re-enable notifications

You can also turn on notifications directly from the app or your device settings.

Option 1: Via Snapchat

Follow the steps mentioned below to do the same on Snapchat:

  1. Open Snapchat and tap on your profile from the top left corner.
  2. Select the settings icon from the top right corner.
  3. Swipe down and tap on Notifications.
  4. Turn the toggle on for the notifications you wish to receive.

This way if you have accidentally disabled notifications, you can get them back.

Option 2: Via Android

Similarly, you can do the same from your Android smartphone:

Note: Not all Android devices have the same interface since they vary from manufacturer to manufacturer. Hence, ensure the correct settings have been selected according to your device’s language. 

  1. Open Settings and tap on Notifications.
  2. Tap on App notifications.
  3. Swipe down and select Snapchat.
  4. Now, turn the toggle on for All Snapchat notifications.

You will start getting the default Snapchat notification sound if it is not working.

Option 3: Via iPhone

You can also do the same from your iPhone:

  1. Open Settings and tap on Notifications.
  2. Swipe down and select Snapchat.
  3. Now, turn the toggle on for Allow Notifications.

That’s it, you will get alerts instantly.

Method 5: Turn off DND and Focus mode

If your Snapchat notification sound not working on your iPhone, you can try disabling the DND mode.

  1. Swipe down from the top right corner to open Control Centre.
  2. Long press on Focus.
  3. Then, tap on Do Not Disturb.

Now you will start getting notifications.

Also Read: What Are Snapchat Streaks? How They Work & More

By following the methods shown in this guide, we hope that now you have understood some of the ways to fix the Snapchat notifications sound not working. Do not hesitate to drop a comment or suggestions in case you have any queries. Keep visiting TechCult to learn more tech-related walkarounds.

title: Snapchat Red Heart Emoji Meaning Explained: What Does It Mean & How to Get
subtitle: Snapchat Red Heart Emoji Meaning Explained: The red heart emoji represents your best friend after snapping for more than 2 weeks
author: Techcult
summary: Snapchat Red Heart Emoji Meaning Explained: The red heart emoji represents your best friend after snapping for more than 2 weeks
content:
Snapchat is known to use emoji-based interactions to communicate with friends and family. Each emoji has a different meaning that signifies how much you react to a user. If you have spotted a red love heart emoji and wondered about its meaning, you’re in the right place. Whether you want to celebrate a snap-streak milestone or decode the emoji significance, we have got you covered. Let’s get started!

  • What Does Red Heart Mean on Snapchat?
  • How to Get Red Heart Emoji on Snapchat
  • Can I Have Multiple Red Heart Emojis on Snapchat?
  • What is the Meaning of Double Red Heart Emoji on Snapchat?

What Does Red Heart Mean on Snapchat?

The red heart emoji represents your number one best friend on Snapchat. It comes beside the username of the person you exchange the most snaps with for more than two weeks and who also ranks you as your top contact. It recognizes the steady bond between you and your friend, indicating that you have interacted the most with them for a long time.

How to Get Red Heart Emoji on Snapchat

You can do several actions to get the heart emoji with a user, such as:

  • Send and receive snaps and chat daily with the same person for at least 14 consecutive days.
  • Boost engagement by adding text, stickers, or filters to your snaps.
  • Regularly view and reply to each other’s Snapchat stories.
  • Join group chats together to increase overall interaction levels.
  • Use the ‘Pin as Your #1 BFF’ feature if you are a Snapchat+ user to manually assign a top friend and bypass snap history.

Can I Have Multiple Red Heart Emojis on Snapchat?

No, Snapchat does not allow more than one user to get the red heart emoji, as only your top BFF can get it mutually.

What is the Meaning of Double Red Heart Emoji on Snapchat?

If you continue being each other’s #1 Best Friend for two months on Snapchat, the single red heart turns into two pink hearts emoji.

Now you will no longer have a difficult time figuring out the meaning behind the red heart emoji on Snapchat after following this guide. For more helpful tips and tricks, stay tuned, and feel free to share your suggestions in the comments below.

title: CtrlOps Review: AI-Powered Linux Server Management Tool (2026)
subtitle: CtrlOps is a local-first desktop app that lets developers manage Linux servers, deploy apps, and debug issues using AI. No DevOps expertise required.
author: Techcult
summary: CtrlOps is a local-first desktop app that lets developers manage Linux servers, deploy apps, and debug issues using AI. No DevOps expertise required.
content:
Managing Linux servers is one of those tasks that sounds straightforward until you are actually doing it at 2 AM with a production outage on your hands, five terminal windows open, and no idea which one is connected to which server. If you have been there, you know the problem. And CtrlOps was built specifically to fix it. This review covers what CtrlOps does, who it is built for, how each feature works in practice, and whether it is worth switching to from your current setup.

  • CtrlOps Review: The AI-Powered Desktop App That Makes Linux Server Management Simple
  • What Is CtrlOps?
  • Who Is CtrlOps Actually For?
  • 7 Key Features Explained
  • 1. Multi-Server Directory
  • 2. AI Terminal
  • 3. One-Click App Deployment
  • 4. Built-In File Manager
  • 5. Infra Monitoring Dashboard
  • 6. Automated Backups
  • 7. SSH Setup Wizard
  • How CtrlOps Handles Security
  • CtrlOps vs. Alternatives
  • Pricing
  • How to Get Started
  • FAQ

CtrlOps Review: The AI-Powered Desktop App That Makes Linux Server Management Simple

What Is CtrlOps?

CtrlOps is a desktop application for macOS, Windows, and Linux that brings all your server management tasks into one place. It connects to any Linux server over SSH and gives you a visual interface for things that would otherwise require memorising and running terminal commands.

The headline features are a multi-server directory, an AI-powered terminal, a built-in file manager, one-click app deployment, and a live infrastructure monitoring dashboard. All of it runs entirely on your local machine. Nothing is stored in the cloud.

The product is built around one core idea: a developer who can write solid code should not need to become a Linux expert just to deploy and manage that code on a server. CtrlOps bridges that gap without removing the terminal for those who want it.

Current stats from the platform:

  • 1,250+ servers under management
  • 8,940+ deployments completed
  • 15,420+ backups executed
  • Average deployment time: under 30 seconds

Who Is CtrlOps Actually For?

CtrlOps targets a specific type of user: technically capable but not a dedicated DevOps specialist.

Freelance developers managing multiple client servers are a natural fit. If you currently have a spreadsheet of IP addresses, a sticky note of SSH commands, and three different apps open to do one deployment, CtrlOps collapses all of that into one window.

Small startup teams where the CTO or a senior developer owns the infrastructure by default are another core use case. When one person knows all the server details and nobody else can cover them during an incident, that is a serious operational risk. CtrlOps solves the knowledge-in-one-person problem by making the infrastructure self-serve for the whole team.

Technical founders who built their own product and need to manage the servers without hiring a DevOps engineer will find the AI terminal and one-click deployment particularly useful. The tool reduces what used to be a 60-minute manual process to something that takes under five minutes.

Agencies managing staging and production for multiple clients can use CtrlOps to organise servers by client name, share the setup across team members, and handle deployments without SSH command knowledge at the developer level.

The tool is not aimed at large enterprise teams with dedicated infrastructure departments. Those teams already have Ansible, Terraform, and full CI/CD pipelines. CtrlOps fills the gap for the 2 to 15 person team that does not have that setup and needs something that works right now.

7 Key Features Explained

1. Multi-Server Directory

The first thing you see when you open CtrlOps is a dashboard of all your connected servers. Each server appears as a named card: you give it a human-readable label like “prod-api” or “client-xyz-staging” rather than staring at raw IP addresses.

One click on the play button connects you instantly. No typing, no IP lookup, no credential retrieval from a spreadsheet. Connection status, last connected time, and server name are shown clearly on each card.

You can connect via standard SSH key or upload a .pem file directly for AWS-style authentication. Server lists can be exported and imported, so onboarding a new team member means sharing a file rather than walking them through a setup session.

This single feature alone fixes what is probably the most common small-team pain point: maintaining a shared Google Sheet or Notion page of server IPs that goes stale, gets corrupted, or requires a degree of trust to share securely. The directory makes the spreadsheet unnecessary.

2. AI Terminal

The AI Terminal is the feature that makes CtrlOps genuinely different from every other SSH client on the market.

It works like this: you type what you want to do in plain English. The AI generates the appropriate shell command. You see the command before it runs, review it, and click approve. The command executes on your server via the live SSH session, and the AI then gives you a human-readable summary of the output.

Some example prompts that work out of the box:

  • “Why is my server slow?”
  • “Check memory and CPU”
  • “Show recent error logs”
  • “Restart the crashed service”
  • “Clean up disk space safely”

The AI has live access to your server’s processes, logs, and metrics. That is the critical difference from copying and pasting logs into ChatGPT in a separate tab. When you ask “why is CPU at 87%?”, the AI is already looking at your actual running processes and gives you a specific answer, not a generic one.

CtrlOps supports multiple AI providers through your own API key. You can connect OpenAI (GPT-4o and others), Google Gemini, Anthropic Claude, or any OpenAI-compatible provider like Groq or local models. You control which model you use and what you pay for AI access. CtrlOps does not mark up or monetise your AI usage.

For power users who do not want to approve every command, there is an Auto-Run mode that skips the approval gate. This is off by default, which is sensible: the default experience keeps a human in the loop before anything touches your server.

The AI Terminal is particularly useful during incidents. A developer who is not a Linux expert can describe a symptom in plain English and get a step-by-step investigation and fix, without needing to know whether they should be running journalctl or dmesg or top.

3. One-Click App Deployment

Deploying a Node.js, React, or Next.js app to a VPS manually is one of the more frustrating experiences in web development. You clone the repo, install the correct Node version, run the build, configure PM2 for process management, set up Nginx as a reverse proxy, open firewall ports, run Certbot for SSL, and then wonder why it is not working. Most developers have to stitch together six or seven different guides to get it right the first time.

CtrlOps replaces all of that with a form.

From the File Manager, click “Add Application” and fill in the following:

  • Application name and environment (Development, Staging, or Production)
  • GitHub repository URL (supports private repos via GitHub token)
  • Node.js version
  • Application type: Node.js, React, Next.js, or build folder
  • Environment variables (paste your entire .env file at once via bulk paste)
  • Domain name
  • SSL via Certbot (toggle on/off)

Click Create, and CtrlOps handles the build, PM2 process setup, Nginx configuration, and SSL certificate installation automatically. Average deployment time is under 30 seconds.

For teams currently paying for Heroku, Render, or Railway to avoid this complexity, this feature alone makes the switch to a cheaper VPS realistic. A Next.js app that costs thousands per month on a managed platform can run on a VPS for a fraction of the price, with CtrlOps handling the deployment complexity that made self-hosting feel too risky.

Also Read: 15 Best IRC Clients for Mac and Linux

4. Built-In File Manager

The File Manager is a full GUI browser for your server’s file system, like Finder or Windows Explorer but for your remote server. It opens as the first tab when you connect to any server.

You can browse the entire directory tree visually, toggle hidden files on or off, search by name, and see item counts per directory. Every file and folder supports download, upload, create, rename, delete, and edit operations from within the interface.

For teams that previously used WinSCP, Cyberduck, or manual SCP commands for file transfers, this removes an entire separate tool from the workflow. Updating an Nginx config, uploading a build artifact, or clearing old log files all happen inside the same application you are already using for SSH access.

5. Infra Monitoring Dashboard

The Infra Details tab gives you a real-time view of CPU usage, RAM status (used, available, swap), disk storage, and a table of all running processes with their CPU and memory percentages.

Two practical one-click actions are available: Clean Cache (clears RAM cache) and Clean Old Buffers (frees up disk buffer memory). These are the kinds of quick fixes that would otherwise require knowing the exact commands and flags to run safely.

For teams without a dedicated monitoring tool, this gives enough visibility to catch problems before users do. You can see that disk is climbing toward full capacity before an app throws 500 errors. You can spot a runaway process eating memory before the server becomes unresponsive.

It is not a replacement for a dedicated monitoring service on large fleets. But for a team managing three to twenty servers, it is exactly the level of visibility needed without the overhead of setting up something like Prometheus and Grafana from scratch.

6. Automated Backups

Automated backups are included as a core feature within each connected server view. You configure the schedule once and CtrlOps handles execution and logging.

This matters because backup setup is the task that most small teams know they should do and almost never actually do. It is genuinely easy to defer until a disk fails. CtrlOps removes the excuse by making it a first-class feature that takes minutes to configure rather than a project in itself.

The dashboard tracks backup history and execution status, so you can verify that backups are running correctly without having to SSH in and check manually.

7. SSH Setup Wizard

For users who are new to SSH or setting up a new machine, CtrlOps includes a guided SSH setup wizard. It walks through SSH installation, key generation, and the exact steps to add your public key to a server, with one-click copy buttons for each key and pre-filled commands for the manual setup path.

This is a small feature but a meaningful one. SSH key setup trips up a lot of developers who are otherwise capable. Having the guidance built into the same tool where you will use the keys removes the context switch to Stack Overflow and reduces setup errors.

How CtrlOps Handles Security

The security model is worth understanding before adopting any tool that touches production servers.

CtrlOps is local-first by design. Every piece of sensitive data: SSH keys, server IPs, credentials, and connection details stays encrypted on your local machine. Nothing is uploaded to CtrlOps servers. The company states they literally cannot see your data.

This is a meaningfully different security posture from tools like Termius, which sync keys to the cloud. If your client contracts or compliance requirements prohibit storing credentials on third-party infrastructure, CtrlOps is compliant where those tools are not.

The AI terminal follows an approve-before-execute model. Every command the AI generates is shown to you before it runs. You see exactly what will be executed, on which server, and you decide whether to run it. This prevents the kind of mistake where an AI confidently generates a dangerous command and runs it without giving you a chance to review it.

CtrlOps only requires an SSH key to connect to your servers. It does not need your AWS IAM credentials, GCP service account, or Azure credentials. The access scope is limited to the server over SSH, which limits the blast radius significantly if anything were to go wrong.

AI provider keys (for the AI Terminal) are encrypted at rest with AES-256 and stored locally. They are never sent to CtrlOps servers.

CtrlOps vs. Alternatives

Here is how CtrlOps sits relative to the tools it most commonly replaces:

vs. PuTTY + WinSCP + separate monitoring + ChatGPT
This is the four-app combination that most solo developers and small teams currently use. CtrlOps replaces all of it with a single application. The time saved from tool-switching alone is significant across a week of work.

vs. Termius
Termius is the most direct comparison as an SSH client. Termius offers clean SSH access and multi-device sync. CtrlOps adds AI-assisted debugging, one-click deployment, a built-in file manager, and infra monitoring that Termius does not have. The other key difference is local vs. cloud: CtrlOps keeps credentials on your machine; Termius syncs them to the cloud.

vs. MobaXterm
MobaXterm is Windows-only and feature-heavy in a way that makes it complex to navigate. CtrlOps is cross-platform, more modern in its interface, and adds the AI terminal layer that MobaXterm lacks.

vs. Ansible/Terraform/full CI/CD pipelines
Enterprise-grade infrastructure tools are a completely different category. They require significant setup time and DevOps knowledge to use correctly. CtrlOps is not competing with these tools for teams that already have them. It is the option for teams that do not have the budget, time, or headcount to implement enterprise tooling and need something that works today.

Pricing

CtrlOps offers a 28-day free trial with no credit card required.

Monthly plan: $3.50/month (approx.) or INR 299/month
Includes unlimited server connections, AI Terminal, advanced File Manager, multi-server fleet management, one-click deployments, simplified user registry, and all updates.

Annual plan: $35/year (approx.) or INR 2,999/year
Everything in the monthly plan plus a 20% discount, priority email support, and early access to new features. Works out to roughly INR 250 per month.

Enterprise: Coming soon
Will include dedicated account management, SLA guarantee (99.9% uptime), custom integrations and API, SSO/team provisioning, and on-premise deployment.

No auto-renewal without notice. No hidden fees.

For context, this is less than the cost of one hour of freelance DevOps work. For a team replacing manual deployments that take 30 to 60 minutes each, the time savings make the pricing straightforward to justify.

How to Get Started

CtrlOps Review: The AI-Powered Desktop App That Makes Linux Server Management Simple

What Is CtrlOps?

CtrlOps is a desktop application for macOS, Windows, and Linux that brings all your server management tasks into one place. It connects to any Linux server over SSH and gives you a visual interface for things that would otherwise require memorising and running terminal commands.

The headline features are a multi-server directory, an AI-powered terminal, a built-in file manager, one-click app deployment, and a live infrastructure monitoring dashboard. All of it runs entirely on your local machine. Nothing is stored in the cloud.

The product is built around one core idea: a developer who can write solid code should not need to become a Linux expert just to deploy and manage that code on a server. CtrlOps bridges that gap without removing the terminal for those who want it.

Current stats from the platform:

  • 1,250+ servers under management
  • 8,940+ deployments completed
  • 15,420+ backups executed
  • Average deployment time: under 30 seconds

Who Is CtrlOps Actually For?

CtrlOps targets a specific type of user: technically capable but not a dedicated DevOps specialist.

Freelance developers managing multiple client servers are a natural fit. If you currently have a spreadsheet of IP addresses, a sticky note of SSH commands, and three different apps open to do one deployment, CtrlOps collapses all of that into one window.

Small startup teams where the CTO or a senior developer owns the infrastructure by default are another core use case. When one person knows all the server details and nobody else can cover them during an incident, that is a serious operational risk. CtrlOps solves the knowledge-in-one-person problem by making the infrastructure self-serve for the whole team.

Technical founders who built their own product and need to manage the servers without hiring a DevOps engineer will find the AI terminal and one-click deployment particularly useful. The tool reduces what used to be a 60-minute manual process to something that takes under five minutes.

Agencies managing staging and production for multiple clients can use CtrlOps to organise servers by client name, share the setup across team members, and handle deployments without SSH command knowledge at the developer level.

The tool is not aimed at large enterprise teams with dedicated infrastructure departments. Those teams already have Ansible, Terraform, and full CI/CD pipelines. CtrlOps fills the gap for the 2 to 15 person team that does not have that setup and needs something that works right now.

The first thing you see when you open CtrlOps is a dashboard of all your connected servers. Each server appears as a named card: you give it a human-readable label like “prod-api” or “client-xyz-staging” rather than staring at raw IP addresses.

One click on the play button connects you instantly. No typing, no IP lookup, no credential retrieval from a spreadsheet. Connection status, last connected time, and server name are shown clearly on each card.

You can connect via standard SSH key or upload a .pem file directly for AWS-style authentication. Server lists can be exported and imported, so onboarding a new team member means sharing a file rather than walking them through a setup session.

This single feature alone fixes what is probably the most common small-team pain point: maintaining a shared Google Sheet or Notion page of server IPs that goes stale, gets corrupted, or requires a degree of trust to share securely. The directory makes the spreadsheet unnecessary.

The AI Terminal is the feature that makes CtrlOps genuinely different from every other SSH client on the market.

It works like this: you type what you want to do in plain English. The AI generates the appropriate shell command. You see the command before it runs, review it, and click approve. The command executes on your server via the live SSH session, and the AI then gives you a human-readable summary of the output.

Some example prompts that work out of the box:

  • “Why is my server slow?”
  • “Check memory and CPU”
  • “Show recent error logs”
  • “Restart the crashed service”
  • “Clean up disk space safely”

The AI has live access to your server’s processes, logs, and metrics. That is the critical difference from copying and pasting logs into ChatGPT in a separate tab. When you ask “why is CPU at 87%?”, the AI is already looking at your actual running processes and gives you a specific answer, not a generic one.

CtrlOps supports multiple AI providers through your own API key. You can connect OpenAI (GPT-4o and others), Google Gemini, Anthropic Claude, or any OpenAI-compatible provider like Groq or local models. For power users who do not want to approve every command, there is an Auto-Run mode that skips the approval gate. This is off by default, which is sensible: the default experience keeps a human in the loop before anything touches your server.

The AI Terminal is particularly useful during incidents. A developer who is not a Linux expert can describe a symptom in plain English and get a step-by-step investigation and fix, without needing to know whether they should be running journalctl or dmesg or top.

Deploying a Node.js, React, or Next.js app to a VPS manually is one of the more frustrating experiences in web development. You clone the repo, install the correct Node version, run the build, configure PM2 for process management, set up Nginx as a reverse proxy, open firewall ports, run Certbot for SSL, and then wonder why it is not working. Most developers have to stitch together six or seven different guides to get it right the first time.

CtrlOps replaces all of that with a form.

From the File Manager, click “Add Application” and fill in the following:

  • Application name and environment (Development, Staging, or Production)
  • GitHub repository URL (supports private repos via GitHub token)
  • Node.js version
  • Application type: Node.js, React, Next.js, or build folder
  • Environment variables (paste your entire .env file at once via bulk paste)
  • Domain name
  • SSL via Certbot (toggle on/off)

Click Create, and CtrlOps handles the build, PM2 process setup, Nginx configuration, and SSL certificate installation automatically. Average deployment time is under 30 seconds.

For teams currently paying for Heroku, Render, or Railway to avoid this complexity, this feature alone makes the switch to a cheaper VPS realistic. A Next.js app that costs thousands per month on a managed platform can run on a VPS for a fraction of the price, with CtrlOps handling the deployment complexity that made self-hosting feel too risky.

The File Manager is a full GUI browser for your server’s file system, like Finder or Windows Explorer but for your remote server. It opens as the first tab when you connect to any server.

For teams that previously used WinSCP, Cyberduck, or manual SCP commands for file transfers, this removes an entire separate tool from the workflow. Updating an Nginx config, uploading a build artifact, or clearing old log files all happen inside the same application you are already using for SSH access.

The Infra Details tab gives you a real-time view of CPU usage, RAM status (used, available, swap), disk storage, and a table of all running processes with their CPU and memory percentages.

For teams without a dedicated monitoring tool, this gives enough visibility to catch problems before users do. You can see that disk is climbing toward full capacity before an app throws 500 errors. You can spot a runaway process eating memory before the server becomes unresponsive.

It is not a replacement for a dedicated monitoring service on large fleets. But for a team managing three to twenty servers, it is exactly the level of visibility needed without the overhead of setting up something like Prometheus and Grafana from scratch.

Automated backups are included as a core feature within each connected server view. You configure the schedule once and CtrlOps handles execution and logging.

This matters because backup setup is the task that most small teams know they should do and almost never actually do. It is genuinely easy to defer until a disk fails. CtrlOps removes the excuse by making it a first-class feature that takes minutes to configure rather than a project in itself.

The dashboard tracks backup history and execution status, so you can verify that backups are running correctly without having to SSH in and check manually.

For users who are new to SSH or setting up a new machine, CtrlOps includes a guided SSH setup wizard. It walks through SSH installation, key generation, and the exact steps to add your public key to a server, with one-click copy buttons for each key and pre-filled commands for the manual setup path.

This is a small feature but a meaningful one. SSH key setup trips up a lot of developers who are otherwise capable. Having the guidance built into the same tool where you will use the keys removes the context switch to Stack Overflow and reduces setup errors.

The security model is worth understanding before adopting any tool that touches production servers.

CtrlOps is local-first by design. Every piece of sensitive data: SSH keys, server IPs, credentials, and connection details stays encrypted on your local machine. Nothing is uploaded to CtrlOps servers. The company states they literally cannot see your data.

This is a meaningfully different security posture from tools like Termius, which sync keys to the cloud. If your client contracts or compliance requirements prohibit storing credentials on third-party infrastructure, CtrlOps is compliant where those tools are not.

title: 13+ Best KeyKey Alternatives for Windows
subtitle: Best KeyKey Alternatives for Windows: TypingMaster, Typesy, RataType, Rapid Typing Tutor, KAZ, and NCHSoftware
author: Techcult
summary: Best KeyKey Alternatives for Windows: TypingMaster, Typesy, RataType, Rapid Typing Tutor, KAZ, and NCHSoftware
content:
If you have been trying to sharpen your typing skills, then you must have heard of KeyKey. The platform has helped hundreds of users get a hand in typing faster and increasing their productivity. But they often feel like some customization or tracking features are missing, making it difficult to fully enjoy the site. Don’t worry, if you are in the quest to find the best KeyKey alternatives for Windows, you’re at the right place! Let’s unravel this mystery.

  • Best KeyKey Alternatives for Windows
  • 1. TypingMaster
  • 2. Typesy
  • 3. RataType
  • 4. Rapid Typing Tutor
  • 5. KeyBlaze
  • 6. NCHSoftware
  • 7. KAZ
  • 8. TypingClub
  • 9. Keybr
  • 10. Monkeytype
  • 11. Typing Test
  • 12. Klavaro Touch Typing Tutor
  • 13. Typing.com
  • 14. ClickClack

Best KeyKey Alternatives for Windows

Now you can enjoy several features that make your typing skills better and better every day.

1. TypingMaster

TypingMaster is one of those classic typing programs that’s been around forever. It’s a desktop app that digs deep into your typing habits and shows you detailed reports on accuracy, speed, and which keys give you trouble. Works completely offline, which is nice. They throw in some games and modules to keep things from getting boring during longer practice sessions.

Features:

  • Adaptive training targets your weak spots.
  • Progress charts track speed improvements.
  • Games make practice sessions fun.

2. Typesy

Typesy is really good for kids, but it works for anyone. It has tasks that actually help with critical and creative thinking, not just typing speed. You start at beginner level and work your way up on one platform. It adjusts to how fast you’re learning and tracks your progress individually.

Features:

  • Single platform from beginner to pro.
  • Adjusts to your personal pace.
  • Keeps kids engaged with fun tasks.

3. RataType

RataType keeps things super simple. Free typing practice with a speed test, and you get a certificate when you hit your goals. People like it because it’s straightforward, even though it doesn’t have as many bells and whistles as other programs. No complicated stuff getting in the way of just practicing, making it one of the best KeyKey alternatives for Windows.

Features:

  • Free typing speed tests available.
  • Earn certificates for achievements.
  • Simple multilingual interface.

4. Rapid Typing Tutor

Rapid Typing Tutor works for both beginners and advanced typists. It has a colorful, game style interface that focuses on where your fingers should go and how fast you’re typing. Real time feedback tells you immediately which keys you’re messing up on, but it keeps things fun instead of feeling like homework. Multi user support is great if you have kids or want to use it in a classroom.

Features:

  • Visual keyboard shows finger positions.
  • Real-time stats track performance.
  • Supports multiple users at once.

5. KeyBlaze

KeyBlaze Typing Tutor from NCH Software has structured lessons that start basic and build up to advanced stuff like numbers and punctuation. Voice guided lessons and a clean interface make it easy for beginners. They include video demos showing proper technique. Games keep it interesting as you go through the lessons.

Features:

  • Guided lessons track your progress.
  • Voice instructions teach technique.
  • Interactive games test skills.

6. NCHSoftware

NCHSoftware is a complete typing tutor with cool features like dictation exercises and certificates you can actually use for job applications. It gives you a skills test at the start to figure out your level and shows your net and gross words per minute. Keyboard highlighting shows you which finger to use during practice, making it one of the best KeyKey alternatives for Windows.

Features:

  • Audio dictation builds listening skills.
  • Highlightsproper finger positions.
  • Certificates prove your skills.

7. KAZ

KAZ offers online typing training for both kids and adults using methods they’ve tested on over 18,000 students in UK centers. Touch typing accuracy improves fast through programs created by RSA and NVQ course experts. It’s set up for special educational needs and works on mobile devices too, so it fits different learning styles.

Features:

  • Programs for kids and adults.
  • Mobile access anywhere.
  • University-tested training method.

8. TypingClub

TypingClub is a web-based typing tutor that makes learning actually enjoyable by mixing interactive stories with practice. You go through guided lessons with videos and animations that show you how to position your hands and move correctly. Makes it way more interesting than basic typing programs. Keeps you motivated while you build actual touch typing skills.

Features:

  • Offers over 600 lessons with visuals.
  • Includes video tutorials for finger placement.
  • Syncs progress with a free account.

9. Keybr

Keybr keeps things simple and focuses on muscle memory. It uses smart algorithms to figure out which letters you struggle with and drills those specifically. The interface is super clean with no distractions, and you get detailed stats on speed, accuracy, and keystroke patterns. Good for people who want serious practice without extra fluff, making it one of the best KeyKey alternatives for Windows.

Features:

  • Adaptive lessons hit weak keys first.
  • Clean interface blocks distractions.
  • Tracks speed and errors live.

10. Monkeytype

Monkeytype is a browser typing platform where you can customize everything. Test lengths, themes, word lists, all of it. The minimal design cuts out all distractions completely. Perfect for daily practice that doesn’t get stale because you can change it up however you want.

Features:

  • Customize tests by time or words.
  • Tracks accuracy and consistency live.
  • Leaderboards for community challenges.

11. Typing Test

Typing Test sets up your practice like an online classroom. You get drills, quizzes, and progress badges as you improve. The web app takes you from beginner to advanced through focused lessons instead of just throwing random tests at you.

Features:

  • Lessons build skills step by step.
  • Games reinforce typing accuracy.
  • Badges track your achievements.

12. Klavaro Touch Typing Tutor

Klavaro is free and works on different platforms. Has structured lessons starting from basic finger placement all the way to advanced speed training. Supports over 20 languages. It’s a desktop program that works offline, so you don’t need the internet for serious training sessions.

Features:

  • Lessons in 20+ languages available.
  • Progress charts show improvement.
  • Runs offline on all major OS.

13. Typing.com

Typing.com is used in schools and offices everywhere, making it one of the best KeyKey alternatives for Windows. Combines lessons, games, and themed sessions with automatic tracking of your WPM and accuracy. You can actually see your progress over time through practice that stays engaging and doesn’t feel like you’re doing the same thing over and over.

Features:

  • Full curriculum from beginner up.
  • Games keep practice interesting.
  • Tracks WPM and accuracy automatically.

14. ClickClack

ClickClack turns typing practice into an actual game with interactive challenges, colorful themes, and smooth gameplay that hooks you. The modern approach makes it kind of addictive while you still get real improvements in your typing speed over time.

Features:

  • Gamified lessons with visual feedback.
  • Daily streaks build habits.
  • Graphs show detailed progress.

Features:

  • Open-source for privacy.

content:
Did you come across a profile picture that inspired you and left you wanting to use it for your own creative projects? Taking someone’s profile picture without their permission can violate their privacy. However, in today’s blog, we will explore some methods that help you figure out how to take someone’s Discord PFP without crossing any boundaries. Sounds like a dream come true, isn’t it? Let’s get started!

  • How to Take Someone’s Discord PFP
  • Method 1: Using Inspect Elements
  • Method 2: Via Discord Bot
  • What Command on Discord Let’s Me See a User’s Avatar?
  • Is There a Way to Save Someone’s Discord Profile If You’re Blocked?
  • Is It Legal to Take Someone’s Discord PFP?

How to Take Someone’s Discord PFP

If you come across a profile picture that you really like and want to save it on your device yourself, there are a few methods you can use to do so. Stay tuned to see how.

Method 1: Using Inspect Elements

You can easily do the same from the Discord web version. Follow the steps below to do the same:

  1. Log into your Discord account and navigate to the user’s profile you want to download the display image.
  2. Right-click on the user’s profile and select the Profile option.
  3. Press the Ctrl + Shift + I keys to open the Inspect Element.
  4. Click on the Selector icon at the top left of the inspect element window or press Ctrl + Shift + C.
  5. Click on the user’s profile picture.
  6. From the highlighted area click on the drop-down arrow.
  7. Then, click on the drop-down arrow next to <svg width=>.
  8. Now, click on the link of the image given next to <img src=.
  9. Double-click on the image link and copy it.
  10. Open the New tab in a browser and paste the link.
  11. Right-click on the image and select Save Image As.

This way you can get any user’s profile picture. 

Method 2: Via Discord Bot

There are several Discord bots available that can help you take someone’s Discord profile picture. Some popular options are dyno, Shiro, and m\Mudae. Here’s how you can use Mudae bot to do so:

  1. Visit the official page of the Mundae bot and click on Invite this bot. 
  2. Select the server of your choice and click on Authorize.
  3. Once the bot is added, go to the Discord server and type $w @username in the message box.
  4. Hit Enter.
  5. Now, click on the Embedded image.
  6. Right-click on the image and select Save Image.

That’s it, you can visit anyone’s profile and get their display image. 

What Command on Discord Let’s Me See a User’s Avatar?

Discord has no built-in command to view a user’s avatar. Instead, you can easily see someone’s avatar by clicking on their username. 

Is There a Way to Save Someone’s Discord Profile If You’re Blocked?

No, if someone has blocked you on Discord, you will not be able to view their profile or profile picture. 

Is It Legal to Take Someone’s Discord PFP?

No, it is generally not legal to take someone’s Discord profile picture without their permission. Discord prioritizes users’ privacy, and taking someone’s PFP is prohibited by their community guidelines.

We hope this article helped you understand how to take someone’s Discord PFP. Let us know your queries or suggestions in the comments section below. Keep visiting Techcult for daily blogs.

title: How to Set Up 24/7 Music Bot on Discord
subtitle: How to Set Up 24/7 Music Bot on Discord: Add 24/7 Music bot on any server, Log in to Discord and visit the server, Select any voice channel.
author: Techcult
summary: How to Set Up 24/7 Music Bot on Discord: Add 24/7 Music bot on any server, Log in to Discord and visit the server, Select any voice channel.
content:
Discord is not only known for providing servers to communicate with other users but also for offering tools you can use to have fun under channels. From memes to trivia bots, the app goes above and beyond to enhance your server’s vibes. You can also add continuous background music to create a fun atmosphere and maintain your server’s energy. So, if you are wondering how to set up a 24/7 music bot on Discord, we’ve got you covered!

  • How to Set Up 24/7 Music Bot on Discord
  • Method 1: Via 24/7 Music Bot
  • Method 2: Via Lofi Radio Bot
  • What are Some of the Commands I Can Use for 24/7 Music Bot?
  • Can a 24/7 Music Bot Impact My Discord Server’s Performance?

How to Set Up 24/7 Music Bot on Discord

Enjoy bopping to some of your favorite tracks between gaming sessions or events with your friends. Let’s see how you can make sure the music never stops!

Method 1: Via 24/7 Music Bot

The 24/7 Music bot is one of the most popular bots designed to play music on your servers. Here’s how you can use it on Discord:

  1. Visit the official page of the 24/7 Music bot and click on Invite.
  2. Select the server of your choice under ADD TO SERVER.
  3. Click on Continue followed by Authorize.
  4. Log in to Discord and click on your selected server.
  5. Now, click on any voice channel.
  6. Type in /play to get the bot to play a random song.
  7. Type in /np to display the currently playing song.
  8. Type in /pause to stop the current track.

With these basic commands, you will be successfully able to use the 24/7 Music bot on Discord.

Method 2: Via Lofi Radio Bot

You can also add the Lofi Radio bot that plays music 24/7 on Lofi songs. Follow the steps mentioned below to do the same:

  1. Open Discord and click on your preferred server.
  2. Click on a voice channel.
  3. Now, click on a server profile and select Server Settings.
  4. Click on App Directory under Apps.
  5. Type in Lofi Radio and select the first bot.
  6. Click on Add App.
  7. Select the server of your choice under ADD TO SERVER.
  8. Click on Continue followed by Authorize.
  9. Go back to your server.
  10. Type in /song to see the currently playing song.
  11. Type in /lofi to ask the bot to join the voice channel and play music continuously.
  12. Type in /stop to stop the music.

Now have fun playing your favorite tunes. 

What are Some of the Commands I Can Use for 24/7 Music Bot?

The 24/7 Music bot offers several commands to choose from such as:

  • /add: To add a song to the queue. This command can only be used if you have purchased the premium plan of the bot.
  • /donators: To display messages from premium+ members.
  • /export-queue: To export your current queue as a file for later use.
  • /import-queue: To import a queue file.
  • /clearqueue: To remove all songs from the queue.
  • /info: To display information about the bot.
  • /leaves: To ask the bot to leave the channel.
  • /permissions: To get or edit permissions for commands or buttons.
  • /remove: To remove a song from your queue. This is a premium-member feature.
  • /rename: To toggle rename a song’s title, artist, or both.
  • /shuffle: To toggle shuffle.
  • /toggle-on-demand-note: To turn the On-demand player off or on.
  • /toggle-radio-auto-np-messages: To enable or disable automatic now-playing messages for internet radios.
  • /toggle-single-np-mode: To enable or disable the single Now-playing message mode. This is a premium-member feature.
  • /volume: To Display or change the volume. This is a premium-member feature.
  • /streamlink: To search for the stream link of a certain radio station.

Can a 24/7 Music Bot Impact My Discord Server’s Performance?

Yes, running a music bot 24/7 can consume bandwidth and affect server performance, especially on low-end devices or servers with many members. Additionally, it also consumes your device’s battery life.

By following the methods shown in this guide, we hope that you can now know how to set up a 24/7 music bot on Discord. Do not hesitate to drop a comment or suggestions in case you have any queries. Keep visiting TechCult to learn more tech-related walkarounds.

How to Ghost Ping on Discord

Ghost pinging on Discord is a technique where you tag someone and then quickly delete the message before they see it, causing their notification to appear without any visible mention. It’s important because it can be used playfully, though it can also be considered a mischievous act if done continuously. Keep reading until the end to ghost ping users.

Method 1: Via Typing Line Message

You can ghost ping any user in a channel by using a specific line message on Discord. Here’s how:

  1. Log in to Discord and go to the server of your choice.
  2. Click on your preferred channel.
  3. Type in your message as the following text snippet: Any message ||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||​||||||||||||@username
  4. Hit Enter.

Your text will get sent without the lines with only the first text, making you ghost ping any user you wish.

Method 2: Via Using @silent

You can also text a user by using the silent feature which will not show them any alert but show that they are mentioned in a channel. Check out the steps do to the same below:

  1. Open Discord and go to your server.
  2. Select any channel.
  3. Type in @silent followed by any message.
  4. Hit Enter.

Discord will not alert the user or group and silently send your message.

Can You Get Caught Ghost Pinging on Discord?

Yes, server admins can review logs or use bots that track deleted messages to catch ghost pings.

Are There Any Consequences for Ghost Pinging on Discord?

Yes, constantly ghost pinging users can lead to warnings, mutes, or bans depending on the server’s rules.

Can I Disable Notifications from Ghost Pings on Discord?

While you can’t disable ghost pings specifically, you can adjust your notification settings to minimize disruptions.

How Do I Know If I’ve Been Ghost Pinged on Discord?

If you receive a notification but can’t find the message, you’ve likely been ghost pinged by someone on Discord.

Can Bots Detect Ghost Pings on Discord?

Yes, some bots are specifically designed to detect and log ghost pings to help admins avoid spam or take action against users.

Is Ghost Pinging Considered Harassment on Discord?

Yes, although legally ghost pining is not a form of harassment, in many servers, repeated ghost pinging is considered as one and can result in disciplinary action.

Can You Undo a Ghost Ping on Discord?

No, once a ghost ping is sent it cannot be taken back as the message has already been deleted.

title: How to Delete a Channel from Discord Server
