summary: How to Delete a Channel from Discord Server: Tap and hold on to the channel, Tap on Edit Channel, Tap on Delete Channel, Tap on Yes to confirm
content:
Managing multiple channels at a time on Discord can make it difficult for you to effectively communicate with your server members. By deleting some of the channels that are inactive or unwanted you can keep your server organized and engaging. In this comprehensive guide, we will discuss steps in detail on how to delete a channel on Discord. So, let’s begin!

  • How to Delete a Channel from Discord Server
  • Can I Delete Multiple Channels at Once on Discord?
  • Can I Recover a Channel Once Deleted on Discord?
  • What Are the Things to Consider Before Deleting a Channel on Discord?
  • Is There a Separate Permission Needed to Delete Channels?
  • Can I Delete a Channel If I Am Not the Owner?

How to Delete a Channel from Discord Server

Discord server channels are important to effectively communicate with members and share information on specific topics. However, if you have too many channels and some are no longer active deleting it can help you declutter your server and improve overall organization.

Below are the step-by-step instructions provided to delete a channel from the Discord server.

On Android

If you are looking to delete a Discord channel using your Android device the process is quick and easy. Just follow these mentioned steps.

  1. Open the Discord app then navigate to the desired server.
  2. Make sure you are on the Home page of Discord.
  3. Find the specific channel you want to delete.
  4. Now, tap and hold on to the channel until a prompt appears.
  5. Tap on Edit Channel.
  6. Scroll all the way down and tap on Delete Channel.
  7. A confirmation pop-up will appear, tap on Yes to confirm.

Now, the channel will be successfully deleted from your discord server.

On Desktop

You can delete a channel with just a few clicks from the web or app version of Discord.

Here’s how you can do it:

  1. Open your desktop browser and visit the Discord login page.
  2. Log in to your Discord account.
  3. Navigate to your server where you have the channel.
  4. Click on the specific channel then click on Edit Channel.
  5. Click on Delete Channel.
  6. A pop-up will appear, stating that this cannot be done, click on Delete Channel.

That’s it, now your channel will be permanently removed from your Discord server, and you cannot recover it.

Can I Delete Multiple Channels at Once on Discord?

No, currently there is no official way to delete multiple channels at once on Discord. You will need to delete each channel manually by accessing the channel settings. Alternatively, you do have the option to delete the entire server if you want to delete all channels at once. We have given a step-by-step guide on how to delete a channel individually from the discord server. Go through this to remove unwanted channels from your server.

Can I Recover a Channel Once Deleted on Discord?

No, once a channel has been deleted from your Discord server, there is no way to recover it, nor can you recover its messages. The platform permanently deletes the channel and does not offer a feature to retrieve it.

What Are the Things to Consider Before Deleting a Channel on Discord?

When deleting a channel on Discord, it is important to consider a few key factors such as:

  • First, ensure you have the necessary permission to delete the channel. If you are not the owner of the channel, make sure to ask the owner to grant you permission to delete the channel.
  • Deleted channels cannot be recovered, so be sure to think carefully before deleting a channel.
  • Inform channel members in advance about your plan before deleting a channel to avoid any confusion.

Is There a Separate Permission Needed to Delete Channels?

Yes, to delete a channel on Discord you do need separate permission within that server. Currently, a Manage Channel permission allows you to edit categories or channels, create new channels, change the positioning of the channel, and delete channels. This permission is allotted to serve administrators or moderators.

Can I Delete a Channel If I Am Not the Owner?

Yes, even if you are not the owner of the channel you can still delete a channel as long as the owner has granted you the specific permissions to do.

title: How to Change Signature in Outlook (Windows, Mac, and Mobile)
subtitle: How to Change Signature in Outlook: Open Outlook, Select Settings, Select Accounts, Click on Signatures, Click on edit, Select Save
author: Techcult
summary: How to Change Signature in Outlook: Open Outlook, Select Settings, Select Accounts, Click on Signatures, Click on edit, Select Save
content:
With millions of businesses using Microsoft 365, Outlook has emerged as the most popular email platform. Your email signature becomes your identity when interacting with clients, coworkers, or other users. If you have recently changed roles or contact information, you must be wondering how to change your signature in Outlook across all devices. Today, we will show you just that. Let’s get started!

  • How to Change Signature in Outlook (Windows, Mac, and Mobile)
  • Method 1: Via Windows
  • Method 2: Via Mac
  • Method 3: Via Mobile

How to Change Signature in Outlook (Windows, Mac, and Mobile)

Maintaining professionalism and uniformity in all of your communications is a must; that’s why you should update the basics.

Method 1: Via Windows

You can easily access Outlook on your PC and change your signature.

  1. Open Outlook and click on File from the top left ribbon.
  2. Click on Settings.
  3. Select Accounts from the left menu.
  4. Click on Signatures.
  5. Click on the edit icon under the current signature.
  6. Type in your new signature in the box.
  7. Then, click on Save.

Your new signature will be updated.

Method 2: Via Mac

Similarly, the same options are available across Mac.

  1. Open Outlook and click on File from the top left menu.
  2. Click on Settings or Preferences if you are running on the older version.
  3. Click on Signatures under Email.
  4. Select any option from Standard, Sent from Outlook for Mac, or Personal.
  5. Then, click on Edit.
  6. Type in the new signature under the Signature Preview box.

Your new signature will be automatically saved.

Method 3: Via Mobile

Lastly, let’s check out how to do the same from your phone:

  1. Open Outlook and tap on your profile in the top left corner.
  2. Select Settings.
  3. Tap on Signature under Quick Settings.
  4. Tap on the edit icon and type in your new signature in the box.
  5. Now, tap on the tick icon at the top right corner.

This way, your signature will successfully be changed.

Also Read: How to Turn Off Text Prediction on Outlook

Now you will no longer have a difficult time figuring out how to change your signature in Outlook across all devices after following this guide. For more helpful tips and tricks, stay tuned, and feel free to share your suggestions in the comments below.

title: How to Turn Off OneDrive on Windows 11
subtitle: How to Turn Off OneDrive on Windows 11: Open OneDrive and click on your profile at the top right corner.Now, click on Sign Out
author: Techcult
summary: How to Turn Off OneDrive on Windows 11: Open OneDrive and click on your profile at the top right corner.Now, click on Sign Out
content:
If you have recently purchased a desktop, you may have noticed that the OneDrive cloud storage service comes built into Windows 11. It automatically syncs your files, photos, and documents across all your devices. Although some may need it, not many users access this storage platform. Therefore, you may wonder how to turn off OneDrive on Windows 11 and get rid of unnecessary space. Let’s get started!

  • How to Turn Off OneDrive on Windows 11
  • Method 1: Unlink Your Account
  • Method 2: Via Startup in Task Manager
  • Method 3: Group Policy Editor
  • Method 4: Registry Editor
  • Method 5: Uninstall OneDrive Settings 
  • Method 6: Uninstall OneDrive Command Prompt
  • Method 7: File Explorer
  • Method 8: Via Control Panel
  • Method 9: Task Scheduler

How to Turn Off OneDrive on Windows 11

Whether you wish to get rid of pop-up notifications or speed up your computer, here are all the ways you can disable OneDrive.

Method 1: Unlink Your Account

You can quickly unlink your account from OneDrive to avoid notifications:

  1. Open OneDrive and click on your profile at the top right corner.
  2. Now, click on Sign Out.

Once you’re logged out, OneDrive will become inactive.

Method 2: Via Startup in Task Manager

You can also turn off the Task Manager.

  1. Open Task Manager and click on Startup apps from the left menu.
  2. Now, right-click on OneDrive and select Disable.

OneDrive will be disabled.

Method 3: Group Policy Editor

Follow the steps to do the same from the Group Policy Editor:

  1. Press the Windows and R keys to open the Run dialog.
  2. Type in gpedit.msc and hit Enter.
  3. Select Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Windows Components.
  4. Click on OneDrive.
  5. Double-click it to open its properties.
  6. Select Enabled.
  7. Click on Apply followed by OK.
  8. Restart the desktop.

This will successfully disable the platform.

Method 4: Registry Editor

You can do so from the Registry Editor:

  1. Press the Windows and R keys to open the Run dialog.
  2. Type in regedit and hit Enter.
  3. Select Yes.
  4. Click on the down arrow under HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE.
  5. Click on the down arrow under SOFTWARE
  6. Click on the down arrow under Microsoft.
  7. Right-click on OneDrive and select New.
  8. Select DWORD (32-bit) Value.
  9. Name the file DisableFileSync.
  10. Then, double-click DisableFileSync.
  11. Type in 1 under its data.
  12. Click on OK.

OneDrive will be uninstalled.

Method 5: Uninstall OneDrive Settings 

Access your settings to do the same:

  1. Open Settings and click on Apps from the left menu.
  2. Click on Installed apps.
  3. Type in OneDrive in the search bar.
  4. Select the three dots beside the app.
  5. Now, select Uninstall.

The app will be uninstalled.

Method 6: Uninstall OneDrive Command Prompt

You can also use different commands to delete the app.

  1. Right-click on the Start button and select Windows Terminal Admin.
  2. Select Yes.
  3. Type in the command %SystemRoot%System32OneDriveSetup.exe /uninstall.
  4. Hit Enter.
  5. Type in the command %SystemRoot%SysWOW64OneDriveSetup.exe /uninstall for 32-bit system.
  6. Hit Enter.
  7. Restart your desktop.

OneDrive will no longer be in your system.

Method 7: File Explorer

Another way to delete the platform is from the File Explorer.

  1. Open File Explorer and click on This PC.
  2. Click on ProgramData.
  3. Select the Microsoft OneDrive folder and hit the Delete button.
  4. Click on Yes.

The files will be successfully deleted.

Method 8: Via Control Panel

You can also find the program in the Control Panel and delete it:

  1. Open the Control Panel and click on Programs.
  2. Select Uninstall a program.
  3. Then, right-click on Microsoft OneDrive and select Uninstall.

That’s it, the program will be removed.

Method 9: Task Scheduler

Lastly, follow the steps to do the same:

  1. Press the Windows and R keys to open the Run dialog.
  2. Type in taskschd.msc and hit Enter.
  3. Click on Task Scheduler Library from the left menu.
  4. Click on OneDrive folders.
  5. Now, select Disable from the right menu for each program.

Now the programs will no longer be active.

Also Read: How to Delete Files on OneDrive

Now you will no longer have a difficult time figuring out how to turn off OneDrive on Windows 11 after following this guide. For more helpful tips and tricks, stay tuned, and feel free to share your suggestions in the comments below.

title: How to Turn Off Text Prediction on Outlook
subtitle: How to Turn Off Text Prediction on Outlook: Click on View Settings, Select Email, Click on Smart Suggestions, Untick Suggest words or phrases as I type under Text predictions
author: Techcult
summary: How to Turn Off Text Prediction on Outlook: Click on View Settings, Select Email, Click on Smart Suggestions, Untick Suggest words or phrases as I typ...
content:
All of us can agree that getting automatic text predictions can become pretty frustrating, especially while sending important mail for work. Unfortunately, several platforms including Outlook have this feature enabled by default to help users save their time. Knowing how to turn off the text prediction on Outlook can help you maintain your personal writing style and prevent any unwanted or inaccurate suggestions from appearing in your emails. So, what are you waiting for? Let’s show you how it’s done!

  • How to Turn Off Text Prediction on Outlook
  • Method 1: Via New Outlook
  • Method 2: Via Old Outlook
  • Why Can’t I Find the Text Prediction Option on Outlook?
  • Are There Keyboard Shortcuts to Use Text Prediction in Outlook?
  • Can You Customize Text Prediction in Outlook?
  • Can You Turn Off Text Prediction for Specific Emails Only in Outlook?

How to Turn Off Text Prediction on Outlook

Now you can maintain your writing style and ensure every word you type is exactly what you wish to say without getting annoying suggestions. Keep reading below to find out your answer.

Method 1: Via New Outlook

Since the interface of the new Outlook is different, here’s how you disable text predictions from the platform:

  1. Log in to your Outlook account from the browser.
  2. Click on View at the top left ribbon. Please note that you can also click on the settings icon in the top right corner.
  3. Click on View Settings.
  4. Select Email.
  5. Click on Smart Suggestions.
  6. Untick on Suggest words or phrases as I type under Text predictions.
  7. Click on Save.

Now you will not get unnecessary suggested replies while writing an email.

Method 2: Via Old Outlook

Follow the steps mentioned below to find the predictive text option from the old Outlook:

  1. Open Outlook and click on File from the top left corner.
  2. Click on Options from the bottom left corner.
  3. Select Mail.
  4. Untick on Show text predictions while typing under Compose messages.
  5. Click on OK.

Why Can’t I Find the Text Prediction Option on Outlook?

If you cannot locate the text prediction feature on Outlook, there can be a couple of reasons, such as:

  • You are using Outlook from the mobile app.
  • You are on Outlook from the web app version, where the feature is not available.

Are There Keyboard Shortcuts to Use Text Prediction in Outlook?

There are no specific keyboard shortcuts to turn text prediction on or off. You can only change this feature from Outlook settings.

Can You Customize Text Prediction in Outlook?

No, you cannot customize text prediction phrases; you can enable or disable the feature as per your preference.

Can You Turn Off Text Prediction for Specific Emails Only in Outlook?

No, disabling this option will be applied to all future emails in Outlook.

Also Read: How to Set Recurring Reminders in Outlook Without Creating Appointments

By following the methods shown in this guide, we hope that now you have figured out how to turn off the text prediction feature on Outlook. Do not hesitate to drop a comment or suggestions in case you have any queries. Keep visiting TechCult to learn more tech-related walkarounds.

If you are new to the platform, navigating it is understandably difficult since it has so much to offer. But if you are figuring it out one click at a time, you’re missing out on some serious speed. That’s why knowing the top Excel shortcut keys and hotkeys is a game-changer. So, let’s show you the magic combos to make life easier!

  • Top Excel Shortcut Keys and Hotkeys
  • Excel Keyboard Shortcuts: Format
  • Excel Keyboard Shortcuts: Formulas And Functions
  • Excel Keyboard Shortcuts: Navigation And Selection
  • Excel Keyboard Shortcuts: Sort And Filter
  • Excel Keyboard Shortcuts: Print
  • Excel Keyboard Shortcuts: VBA And Macros
  • Excel Keyboard Shortcuts: Workbooks And Worksheets

Top Excel Shortcut Keys and Hotkeys

Whether you’re a student, an accountant, or a data nerd, these shortcuts can completely change how you use Excel.

  • Ctrl + Z: Undo the last action.
  • F11: Insert a chart in a new sheet.
  • Ctrl + H: Display the find and replace with the Replace tab selected.
  • Shift + Space: Select Table row.
  • Alt + F1: Insert Embedded chart.
  • Ctrl + Shift + L: Toggle Auto filter.
  • Ctrl + V: Paste the Content from the clipboard.
  • Ctrl + 6: Hide or show objects.
  • Alt + F8: Open the Macro Dialog box.
  • Ctrl + Y: Redo the last action.
  • Ctrl + D: Duplicate object, Formula, Text.
  • F4: Repeat the last action.
  • Ctrl + F: Display the find and replace with the find tab selected.
  • Alt + (Arrow down button): Enable Filter.
  • Ctrl + A: Select the table when the active cell is in the table with this top Excel shortcut keys.
  • Alt + F11: Open VBA Editor.
  • Ctrl + Alt + V: Display the paste special dialog box.
  • Shift + F4: Find the next match.
  • F1: Open Help.
  • Ctrl + Shift + F4: Find the previous match.
  • Alt + ‘: Open the modify cell style dialog box.
  • Ctrl + T or Ctrl + L: Create Table.
  • F7: Run Spellcheck.
  • Alt + C: Clear Slicer Filter.
  • Ctrl + X: Cut the selected data.
  • Ctrl + C: Copy the Selected data.
  • Alt Space: Display control menu.
  • Shift + F10: Show right-click menu.
  • Alt: Snap to grid.
  • Ctrl + Space: Select Table column.

Excel Keyboard Shortcuts: Format

Now that you are done with basic shortcuts, let’s take a look at these top Excel shortcut keys for formatting style:

  • Alt + H + AC: Align text to the center (between left and right) of the cell.
  • Alt + H + 0: Increase the number of decimals displayed.
  • Alt + H + AL: Align text to the left of the cell.
  • Alt + B: Within the Border tab of the Format Cells dialog box, add/remove the bottom border.
  • Alt + H + AB: Align text to the bottom of the cell.
  • (Ctrl + Alt + V) + T or Alt + H + V + R: Paste format.
  • Alt + H: Within Border tab of Format Cells dialog box, and when more than 1 row is selected, add/remove horizontal interior border.
  • Alt + H + 9: Decrease the number of decimals displayed.
  • Alt + H + AN: Choose accounting format.
  • Alt + H + B + A: Apply borders to all sides of selected cells.
  • Ctrl + Shift + !: Format numbers with two decimal places and thousand separators.
  • Alt + H + M + M: Merge selected cells into one.
  • Ctrl + 5: Toggle strikethrough text formatting.
  • Alt + H + L + R: Open the Conditional Formatting Rules Manager.
  • Ctrl + Shift + #: Apply date formatting (day/month/year).
  • Alt + H + O + I: Automatically adjust column width to fit content.
  • Ctrl + T: Create a new table from selected data.
  • Alt + H + H + N: Remove fill color from selected cells.
  • Ctrl + Shift + ~: Reset cells to General number format.
  • Alt + H + FQ + V: Rotate text vertically in cells.
  • Ctrl + Alt + V + W: Adjust pasted content to match destination column widths.
  • Alt + H + 9: Reduce decimal places in numbers.
  • Ctrl + Shift + F: Open Font formatting options.
  • Alt + H + W: Enable text wrapping in cells.
  • Ctrl + Shift + $: Apply currency formatting with parentheses for negatives.
  • Alt + H + B + S: Add outside borders to selection.
  • F4: Repeat your last action.
  • Alt + H + J + N: Create a new cell style.
  • Ctrl + Shift + &: Add outer borders to selected cells.
  • Alt + H + L + C + S: Clear conditional formatting rules from selected cells.
  • Ctrl + U: Toggle underline text formatting.
  • Alt + H + O + A: Auto-adjust row height to fit content.
  • Ctrl + Shift + %: Format values as percentages without decimals.
  • Alt + H + B + N: Remove all borders from selection.
  • Ctrl + 1: Open full Format Cells dialog.
  • Alt + H + FC: Open font color selection menu.
  • Ctrl + Shift + @: Apply time formatting (HH: MM AM/PM).
  • Alt + H + M + U: Unmerge previously merged cells.
  • Ctrl + B: Toggle bold text formatting.
  • Alt + H + 6: Increase indent.
  • (Ctrl + Alt + V) + W or Alt + H + V + W: Paste column widths.
  • Alt + H + AM: Align text to the middle (between the top and bottom) of the cell.
  • Alt + H + 3 + D: Apply or remove double underlining.
  • Alt + D: Within Border tab of Format Cells dialog box, add/remove downward diagonal border.
  • Alt + H + 5: Decrease indent.
  • (Ctrl + Alt + V) + G or Alt + H + V + G: Paste merging the conditional formatting of the destination and source ranges.
  • Alt + H + AN + M: Display the Format Cells dialog box with the Number tab and the Accounting category selected.
  • Alt + H + B + U: Top and double bottom border.
  • Alt + H + B + H: Thick bottom border.
  • Alt + H + B + R: Right Border.
  • Alt + H + B + I: Choose border line color.
  • Alt + H + AR: Align text to the right of the cell.
  • Alt + H + B + M: Display the Format Cells dialog box with the Border tab selected.
  • Alt + H + B + G: Draw border grid.
  • Alt + H + B + A: All Borders.
  • Alt + H + B + O: Bottom Border.
  • Alt + H + B + E: Erase border.
  • Alt + H + AT: Align text to the top of the cell.
  • Alt + H + B + T: Thick box border.
  • Alt + H + B: Expand Borders drop-down menu.
  • Alt + H + B + L: Left Border.
  • Alt + H + B + D: Top and bottom border.
  • Alt + H + B + S or Ctrl + Shift + 7: Outside border.
  • Alt + H + B + C: Top and thick bottom border.
  • Alt + H + B + N or Ctrl + Shift + –: No Border.
  • Alt + H + B + P: Top Border.
  • Alt + H + B + W: Draw border.
  • Alt + H + B + B: Bottom double border.
  • Alt + H + FQ + V: Rotate text so that it is vertical.
  • Alt + H + FK: Decrease the font size by 1 point.
  • Alt + H + L + C + S: Clear conditional formatting rules from selected cells.
  • Alt + H + FC: Expand Font Color drop-down menu.
  • Alt + H + FQ + M or Alt + H + FA: Display the Format Cells dialog box with the Alignment tab selected.
  • Alt + H + FF: Change the font face.
  • Alt + H + H + N: Apply no fill color to current cell selection.
  • Alt + H + B + Y: Choose border line style.
  • Alt + H + L + C + E: Clear conditional formatting rules from the entire worksheet.
  • Alt + H + FS: Change the font size.
  • Alt + H + FQ + D: Rotate text down.
  • Alt + H + FG: Increase the font size by 1 point.
  • Alt + H + J + N: Display the Style dialog box to create a new cell style.
  • Alt + H + E + F: Clear formatting.
  • Alt + H + FM: Display the Format Cells dialog box with the Number tab selected.
  • Alt + H + FQ + O: Rotate text in an angle counterclockwise.
  • Alt + H + FN: Display the Format Cells dialog box with the Font tab selected with this top Excel shortcut keys.
  • Alt + H + FP: Activate the Format Painter.
  • Alt + H + K: Format number with a thousand’s comma (,) separator.
  • Alt + H + L + D: Expand the menu to set a conditional formatting rule using data bars with gradient or solid fill.
  • Alt + H + FQ + L: Rotate text counterclockwise.
  • Alt + H + J: Expand the Cell Styles menu.
  • Alt + H + H: Expand Fill Color drop-down menu.
  • Alt + H + FQ + U: Rotate text up.
  • Alt + H + J + M: Display the Merge Styles dialog box to merge (copy) cell styles from another workbook.
  • Alt + H + FC: Choose font color.
  • Alt + H + L + C + P: Clear conditional formatting rules from the selected PivotTable (active when cell is within PivotTable).
  • Alt + H + L + C + T: Clear conditional formatting rules from the selected table (active when a cell is within a table).
  • Alt + H + L + H + G: Display the Greater Than dialog box for conditional formatting.
  • Alt + H + M + U: Unmerge cells.
  • Alt + H + O + I: Auto-fit column width.
  • Alt + H + L + H + D: Display the Duplicate Values dialog box.
  • Alt + H + L + T + P: Display the Top 10% dialog box.
  • Alt + H + L + H + M: Display the New Conditional Formatting Rule dialog box (Format only cells that contain).
  • Alt + H + T + N: Display the New Table Style dialog box.
  • Alt + H + L + T + B: Display the Bottom 10 Items dialog box.
  • Alt + H + L + D + M: Display the New Conditional Formatting Rule dialog box (Format all cells based on values).
  • Alt + H + M + A: Merge across cells.
  • Alt + H + L + H + E: Display the Equal To dialog box.
  • Alt + H + O + W: Display the Column Width dialog box.
  • Alt + H + L + I: Expand the icon sets menu for conditional formatting.
  • Alt + H + L + H + A: Display the A Data Occurring dialog box.
  • Alt + H + L + T + V: Display the Below Average dialog box.
  • Alt + H + W: Wrap text.
  • Alt + H + L + T + M: Display the New Conditional Formatting Rule dialog box (top/bottom ranked values).
  • Alt + H + L + H + B: Display the Between dialog box.
  • Alt + H + L + S: Expand the color scales menu for conditional formatting.
  • Alt + H + O + A: Auto-fit row height.
  • Alt + H + L + T + O: Display the Bottom 10% dialog box.
  • Alt + H + L + H + L: Display the Less Than dialog box.
  • Alt + H + M + M: Merge cells.
  • Alt + H + L + N: Display the New Conditional Formatting Rule dialog box.
  • Alt + H + L + R: Display the Conditional Formatting Rules Manager.
  • Alt + H + L + T + T: Display the Top 10 Items dialog box.
  • Alt + A + G + G: Display the Text That Contains dialog box.
  • Alt + H + N: Choose number format.
  • Alt + H + O + H: Display the Row Height dialog box.
  • Alt + H + T: Expand Format as Table menu.
  • Alt + H + T + P: Display the New PivotTable Style dialog box.
  • Alt + L: Add/remove left border.
  • Alt + R: Add/remove right border.
  • Alt + T: Add/remove top border.
  • Alt + V: Add/remove vertical interior border.
  • Ctrl + Shift + @: Apply time format (HH:MM AM/PM).
  • Ctrl + 5: Toggle strikethrough formatting.
  • Ctrl + Shift + !: Apply number format (2 decimals, 1000 separator).
  • F4: Repeat last action.
  • Ctrl + U: Toggle underlining.
  • Ctrl + Shift + $: Apply currency format.
  • Ctrl + I: Toggle italics.
  • Ctrl + Shift + ^: Apply scientific notation.
  • Ctrl + B: Toggle bold formatting.
  • Ctrl + Shift + ~: Reset to General format.
  • Ctrl + Shift + &: Add outer borders.
  • Ctrl + 1: Open Format Cells dialog.
  • Ctrl + T: Create table.
  • Ctrl + Shift + _: Remove borders.
  • Ctrl + Shift + %: Apply percentage format.
  • Ctrl + Shift + #: Apply date format.
  • Ctrl + Shift + F: Open Font formatting.

Excel Keyboard Shortcuts: Formulas And Functions

Let’s take a look at the top Excel shortcut keys related to formulas and functions:

  • (Ctrl + Alt + V) + F: Paste formulas only.
  • (Ctrl + Alt + V) + R: Paste formulas with number formatting.
  • (Ctrl + Alt + V) + L: Paste data links.
  • =: Start a new formula.
  • Ctrl + Shift + Enter: Enter as array formula.
  • F4: Cycle through reference types (absolute/relative).
  • Shift + F3: Open Insert Function dialog.
  • Alt + =: Insert AutoSum.
  • Alt + H + U + A: Calculate average.
  • Alt + H + U + C: Count numbers.
  • Alt + H + U + I: Find minimum value.
  • Alt + H + U + M: Find maximum value.
  • Alt + M + P: Trace precedents.
  • Alt + M + D: Trace dependents.
  • Alt + M + A + A: Remove audit arrows.
  • Ctrl + F3: Open Name Manager.
  • Ctrl + Shift + F3: Create names from selection.
  • F3: Paste named ranges.
  • F9: Calculate all workbooks.
  • Shift + F9: Calculate active sheet.
  • Ctrl + Alt + F9: Force full calculation.
  • Ctrl + A: Show function arguments.
  • Ctrl + Shift + A: Insert arguments.
  • Alt + Shift + F10: Show error menu.
  • Tab: Complete formula and move right.
  • Shift + Tab: Complete formula and move left.

Excel Keyboard Shortcuts: Navigation And Selection

Now let’s take a look at some top Excel shortcut keys for navigation:

  • Here’s your full list, shuffled and paraphrased to match the same bold-until-colon style with a clear, professional structure:
  • Alt + Tab: Cycle through open workbooks and switch to the next one.
  • Ctrl + . : When multiple cells are selected, move the active cell in a clockwise direction around the corners.
  • Alt + F: Open the Backstage View.
  • Ctrl + [ or F5 + (Alt + S) + P: Jump to the direct precedents of a formula within the current worksheet.
  • Ctrl + Shift + * or F5 + (Alt + S) + R: Select the entire data region around the active cell.
  • Alt + A to Alt + Z: Inside dialog boxes, activate a control or toggle checkboxes.
  • Ctrl + Arrow Keys: Navigate quickly to the edge of the current data region.
  • Ctrl + ] or F5 + (Alt + S) + D: Go to the direct dependents of a selected cell.
  • Ctrl + F or Shift + F5 or Alt + H + F + D + F: Open the Find and Replace window with the Find tab highlighted.
  • Alt + Down Arrow: Show the AutoComplete or AutoFilter list inside a cell, or expand a dropdown in a dialog box.
  • Ctrl + Shift + Spacebar or Ctrl + A: Select the data area; press repeatedly to select the entire worksheet or all objects.
  • Ctrl + Home then Ctrl + Shift + End: Select everything from the first to the last used cell in the sheet.
  • Ctrl + End or F5 + (Alt + S) + S: Go to the last cell that contains data (the lowest and right-most used cell).
  • Ctrl + Backspace: Return the view to the active cell, no matter where the scroll is.
  • Alt: Close an open dropdown in AutoFilter or a dialog box.
  • Ctrl + H or Alt + H + FD + R: Launch the Replace tab in the Find and Replace dialog.
  • Ctrl + Left-Click: Add non-adjacent cells or sheets to your current selection.
  • Ctrl + End: If editing a cell, move the cursor to the end of its contents.
  • Arrow Keys: Navigate between cells, tabs, menus, dropdown items, or options depending on the current context.
  • Ctrl + G or F5 or Alt + H + F + D + G: Open the Go To dialog box.
  • Alt + Up Arrow: Close the AutoComplete list in a cell and use this top Excel shortcut keys.
  • Alt + ; or F5 + (Alt + S) +Y: Select only the visible (unfiltered) cells in the range.
  • Alt + Page Down / Page Up: Move one screen right or left within the worksheet.
  • Ctrl + F6: Switch between open workbook windows.
  • Ctrl + Home: Jump to the top-left cell (A1) or to the start of the cell content if editing.
  • Ctrl + Shift + F4: Jump to the previous instance when searching for a match.
  • Ctrl + Space: Instantly select the entire column of the currently active cell.
  • Ctrl + Shift + { or F5 → Alt + S → D → L: Highlight all cells that are direct and indirect precedents to the current cell.
  • Ctrl + Shift + Tab: Move to the previous workbook window, or shift to the previous tab in a dialog box.
  • Ctrl + Shift + Page Up / Page Down: Select the current sheet along with the one before (left) or after (right) it.
  • Ctrl + Page Up / Page Down: Quickly switch between sheets — move left or right.
  • Ctrl + Shift + O or F5 → Alt + S → C or Alt + H → F → D → M: Navigate directly to all cells that contain comments.
  • Ctrl + Shift + Arrow Keys: Expand selection to the data edge in that direction, or (within a cell) select entire words to the left or right.
  • Ctrl + Shift + Home: Extend selection up to the very first cell in the worksheet, or within a cell/formula bar, select from the cursor to the start of content.
  • Ctrl + Shift + End: Select from the current cell all the way to the bottom-right of the used data area, or inside a cell/formula bar, highlight from cursor to end of the content.
  • Ctrl + Shift + } or F5 → Alt + S → P → L: Highlight all dependent cells — both direct and indirect — related to the current formula.
  • Ctrl + Tab: Cycle forward through open workbook windows or tabs in a dialog box.
  • F8: Toggle Extend Selection mode on or off to easily expand your selection using arrow keys.
  • F6: Rotate focus between key elements like the worksheet area, ribbon, task pane, and zoom controls
  • Esc: Cancel the current action and close menus, dialogs, or message boxes. Also used to deselect objects.
  • F1: Open the Help Task Pane. If a command is selected, Help displays the relevant topic.
  • Left Mouse Button + Shift: Add adjacent cells or worksheets to the current selection.
  • Page Down / Page Up: Scroll one screen down or one screen up in the worksheet.
  • Shift + Arrow Keys: Extend the selection by one cell. Inside a cell, select or extend the selection by one character left or right.
  • Shift + Backspace: When multiple cells are selected, reduce selection to only the active cell.
  • Shift + End: Select from the current position to the end of the row inside a cell.
  • Shift + F10: Open the Context (right-click) menu for the selected item.
  • Shift + F4: Repeat the last Find action or find the next match.
  • Shift + F6: Cycle focus between worksheet, Zoom controls, Task pane, and Ribbon (includes split panes if active).
  • Shift + F8: Add a non-adjacent range to the current selection. Use arrow keys to move the cursor and Shift + Arrow Keys to select the range.
  • Shift + Home: Select from the current position to the start of the row. Inside a cell, select from the cursor to the beginning of the line.
  • Shift + Page Down / Shift + Page Up: Extend selection by one screen down or one screen up.
  • Shift + Space: Select the active row. In tables, the first press selects the active row in the table; pressing again selects the entire worksheet row.
  • Shift + Tab: Move one cell left in a worksheet or to the previous unlocked cell in a protected worksheet. Move the active cell left within a selection. Navigate to the previous option or option group in dialog boxes or the Ribbon.
  • Spacebar: In dialog boxes, activate the selected button or toggle checkboxes. In the Ribbon, activate the selected control or open the selected menu/gallery.
  • Tab: Move one cell right in a worksheet or to the next unlocked cell in a protected worksheet. Move the active cell right within a selection. Navigate to the next option or option group in dialog boxes or the Ribbon.
  • Alt + N + V: PivotTable

Excel Keyboard Shortcuts: Sort And Filter

Check out these Excel shortcut keys for sort and filter:

  • Alt + A + V + V: Open the Data Validation settings dialog.
  • Ctrl + Shift + L or Alt + H + S + F: Toggle filters on or off in the current range.
  • Alt + A + SA or Alt + H + S + S: Sort data from smallest to largest.
  • Alt + H + S + C: Remove any applied filters.
  • Ctrl + Alt + L or Alt + H + S + Y: Refresh and reapply the current filter and sort criteria.
  • Alt + A + SD or Alt + H + S + O: Sort data from largest to smallest.
  • Alt + A + SS or Alt + H + S + U: Bring up the Sort dialog box.
  • Alt + A + Q: Launch the Advanced Filter tool.

Excel Keyboard Shortcuts: Print

Follow these shortcuts to print information in Excel:

  • Alt + P + S + P: Launch the dialog box for Page Setup options.
  • Ctrl + P: Access the Print tab within the Backstage View to print documents.
  • Alt + P + R + S: Define the Print Area for your worksheet.
  • Ctrl + F2: Preview the print layout in the Print Preview section of the Backstage View.

Excel Keyboard Shortcuts: VBA And Macros

VBAs and Macros have their own set of shortcuts too:

  • Alt + F11: Open the Visual Basic Editor if it’s closed, or switch between Excel and the Editor if it’s already open.
  • Alt + W + M + U: Activate Relative References mode for macros.
  • Ctrl + G: Show the Immediate Window inside the Visual Basic Editor.
  • F2: Open the Object Browser within the Visual Basic Editor.
  • Alt + L + I: Expand the menu for inserting Form Controls and ActiveX Controls.
  • Alt + F8 or Alt + W + M + V: Open the Macro dialog box.
  • Alt + W + M + R: Start recording a new macro.
  • F5: Run the selected macro inside the Visual Basic Editor.

Excel Keyboard Shortcuts: Workbooks And Worksheets

Lastly, look at these top Excel shortcut keys for worksheet:

  • Ctrl + F7: Activate the Move command on the current workbook window (if not maximized). Use arrow keys to move, then Enter to confirm or Esc to cancel.
  • Ctrl + F12: Open the Open dialog box.
  • Alt + H + O + U + S: Hide the active worksheet.
  • Alt + H + D + S or Alt + E + L: Delete the active worksheet.
  • Ctrl + S or Shift + F12: Save the current file with the existing name and location.
  • Ctrl + N: Create a new blank workbook.
  • Alt + H + O + T + N: Remove color from the current worksheet tab.
  • Ctrl + F11: Insert a new Macro sheet.
  • Alt + H + O + R or Alt + O + H + R: Rename the active worksheet.
  • Ctrl + W: Close the selected workbook.
  • Shift + F11 or Alt + H + I + S: Insert a new worksheet in the current workbook.
  • Alt + H + O + M: Open the Move or Copy worksheet dialog box.
  • Alt + H + O + U + H: Open the Unhide worksheet dialog box.
  • Ctrl + F9: Minimize the current workbook window.
  • Ctrl + F8: Activate the Resize command on the active workbook window (if not maximized). Use arrow keys to resize, Enter to confirm, Esc to cancel.
  • Alt + H + O + T: Open the Tab Color menu.
  • F12 or Alt + F2: Open the Save As dialog box.
  • Ctrl + F4: Close the current workbook window.
  • Ctrl + O: Open the Open tab in Backstage View to open a workbook.
  • Alt + Shift + F1: Insert a new worksheet.

Also Read: 12 Shortcuts to Open Task Manager in Windows 10/11

Now you will no longer have a difficult time figuring out the top Excel shortcut keys after following this guide. For more helpful tips and tricks, stay tuned, and feel free to share your suggestions in the comments below.

title: How to Get a Microsoft Store Student Discount
subtitle: How to Get a Microsoft Store Student Discount: Visit Microsoft Student discount, Select Shop with discount, Enter student ID, Select Shop now
author: Techcult
summary: How to Get a Microsoft Store Student Discount: Visit Microsoft Student discount, Select Shop with discount, Enter student ID, Select Shop now
content:
Between assignments, late-night study sessions, and virtual lectures, students rely on tech more than ever. Microsoft gets that, so it offers helpful tools like Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Copilot. But did you know that if you’re a student, you can get these productive tools at a great discount? Let’s show you how to get a Microsoft Store student discount and make the most of your budget!

  • How to Get a Microsoft Store Student Discount
  • Method 1: Via Microsoft Online Store
  • Method 2: Via Microsoft Offline Store
  • How Much is the Student Discount for Microsoft Products?
  • Who is Eligible for the Microsoft Student Discount?
  • What Microsoft Tools are Free for Students?

How to Get a Microsoft Store Student Discount

Whether you’re looking for a new Surface, a laptop upgrade, or accessories for class, now you can grab those academic savings without breaking a sweat.

Method 1: Via Microsoft Online Store

  1. Visit the official website of Microsoft Student and Military discount.
  2. Click on Shop with discount.
  3. Enter your student email address and credentials.
  4. Select OK after your authentication is approved.
  5. Scroll down and click on Shop now under any goods or services of your choice.
  6. Then, click on Next.
  7. Select specifications for the device and click on Next.
  8. Click on Add items to cart.
  9. Now, select Checkout.
  10. Enter your payment method and complete the purchase.

This way, you can get the best deals available for students.

Method 2: Via Microsoft Offline Store

Similarly, you can also visit a physical Microsoft Store and get discounted items as a student. Just remember to carry the physical student ID during the time of checkout and present it to the cashier. Additionally, you must have an account with Microsoft to confirm your status.

How Much is the Student Discount for Microsoft Products?

Students can get up to 10% off on selected products and online services if they are eligible for the discount. However, the student discount cannot be combined with other offers. Furthermore, Microsoft states that you will not be eligible for an extra student discount if the product currently has a discount greater than 10%.

Who is Eligible for the Microsoft Student Discount?

The student discount is available to K-12 students from ages 5 to 18, as well as college students, instructors, and parents. The education discount is only available to full-time and part-time students, instructors, and parents making purchases on behalf of students and school personnel. Active, retired, and former military personnel and their families are also eligible.

What Microsoft Tools are Free for Students?

There are several basic tools free for students, such as:

  • Word
  • Excel
  • PowerPoint
  • OneNote
  • Microsoft Teams
  • Copilot Chat
  • OneDrive
  • Outlook
  • SharePoint
  • Microsoft Planner
  • Other classroom tools

Also Read: How to Redeem Microsoft Reward Points on Xbox Series X|S 

Now you will no longer have a difficult time figuring out how to get a Microsoft Store student discount after following this guide. For more helpful tips and tricks, stay tuned, and feel free to share your suggestions in the comments below.

title: How to Use Bing Rewards Dashboard
subtitle: How to Use Bing Rewards Dashboard: Visit Microsoft Rewards website, Click on Go to the dashboard, Click on Status to see information
author: Techcult
summary: How to Use Bing Rewards Dashboard: Visit Microsoft Rewards website, Click on Go to the dashboard, Click on Status to see information
content:
Ever wasted your time scrolling on the internet and felt guilty of not being productive? You’re not alone. But what if we tell you, you can turn everyday web searches into real-world perks? With Bing Rewards, users earn points just by searching the web, completing quizzes, and turning them into real-world value. So, if you’re ready to start earning, you’ll need to know all about the Bing Rewards dashboard, and you can earn these perks. Let’s find out below!

  • How to Use Bing Rewards Dashboard
  • Why is Bing Rewards Not Working?
  • What is Eligibility Criteria for Getting Microsoft Bing Rewards?

How to Use Bing Rewards Dashboard

By using the Bing dash, you can check out how many rewards you have or what perks is available for you to enjoy.

  1. Visit the official Microsoft Rewards website and sign in using your credentials.
  2. Click on Go to the dashboard.
  3. Click on Earn from the top ribbon to start getting points.
  4. Scroll down and select an activity to earn points.
  5. Click on Redeem from the top ribbon to use points and get perks.
  6. Click on Status to check your current level, points earned as well as redeemed.

This way, you can sign in to your Bing Rewards dashboard and check all the information easily.

Why is Bing Rewards Not Working?

There can be several reasons behind your rewards not being processed:

  • Ad Blockers or VPNs interfering
  • Browser compatibility issues
  • Search cooldown periods initiated
  • Account or app glitches
  • Reward eligibility issue

What is Eligibility Criteria for Getting Microsoft Bing Rewards?

Here are some things users have to be aware of to get their Bing rewards:

  • Have a valid Microsoft account
  • Be at least 13 years old (or the minimum age in your region)
  • Must reside in a participating country or region
  • Use Bing while signed into your Microsoft account
  • Must not use automated search tools or bots
  • Comply with Microsoft Rewards terms and conditions

Also Read: What Are Bing Rewards & How to Use Them

Now you will no longer have a difficult time figuring out know about the Bing Rewards dashboard and Bing Dash Rewards after following this guide. For more helpful tips and tricks, stay tuned, and feel free to share your suggestions in the comments below.

title: What Are Bing Rewards & How to Use Them
subtitle: What Are Bing Rewards & How to Use Them: Bing Rewards is a loyalty program that allows users to get points by Microsoft services
author: Techcult
summary: What Are Bing Rewards & How to Use Them: Bing Rewards is a loyalty program that allows users to get points by Microsoft services
content:
Scrolling in your browser can be more rewarding than you’d think. Did you know Bing Rewards lets users earn points simply by using it for everyday searches? After knowing this, you may wonder what Bing Rewards are and how you can use them. Ready to make your clicks count? The wait is over, let’s get you the answer in this guide!

  • What Are Bing Rewards?
  • Features and Benefits of Bing Rewards
  • Bing Rewards Loyalty Levels: Member, Silver & Gold Benefits
  • What Can I Redeem Xbox Rewards Points For?

What Are Bing Rewards?

Bing Rewards, now known as Microsoft Rewards, is a loyalty program that allows users to accrue points by using goods and services provided by Microsoft, which include Bing search. You use Bing to gain points by completing specific tasks each day. Once you have enough points, you can exchange them for different incentives like gift cards, lottery tickets, or donations to causes. Additionally, users can receive a discount for the redeemed rewards if they accumulate enough points each month. This means that if you stay consistent, you can get the same amount of earnings with fewer points.

Features and Benefits of Bing Rewards

Let’s take a look at the key features of Bing and why you should use it.

  • No Extra Cost: Just search as usual and get rewarded.
  • Earn Points for Searching: Use Bing like normal, and you’ll rack up points over time.
  • Redeem for Real Rewards: Cash in points for Microsoft Store credits, Xbox gift cards, or even donations to charity.
  • Flexible Rewards: Choose from a variety of gift cards or sweepstakes entries.
  • Easy to Use: Track points right from your dashboard and redeem with a few clicks.
  • Points for Searching: Earn credits simply by using Bing to search the web.
  • Daily Sets and Bonuses: Get extra points by completing daily tasks, quizzes, and offers.
  • Microsoft Ecosystem Integration: Linked with your Microsoft account, making it seamless to earn across devices.

Bing Rewards Loyalty Levels: Member, Silver & Gold Benefits

Bing Rewards gives loyal users extra perks as they climb up the membership ladder, with each level unlocking more benefits the more you engage.

1. Member (Starting Tier)

  • Entry-level access for new users.
  • Earn credits by searching with Bing and completing daily offers.

2. Silver (Mid-Tier Benefits)

  • Unlocked after completing the Welcome to Rewards tour, redeeming your first reward, and earning 200+ lifetime credits.
  • Bonus perk: Get a 50-credit boost upon reaching Silver.

3. Gold (Top-Tier Advantages)

  • Reach Gold status by earning 750+ lifetime credits and performing 150+ qualifying searches per month.
  • Exclusive discount: Enjoy up to 10% off when redeeming rewards.

What Can I Redeem Xbox Rewards Points For?

Points can be redeemed for:

  • Digital gift cards
  • Points/miles for airline and hotel loyalty programs
  • Sweepstakes entries
  • In-game content
  • Prints and photobooks from Shutterfly
  • Xbox Game Pass memberships.
  • Gift cards for Amazon, Burger King, Groupon, IHOP, iTunes, Sephora, Starbucks, and other businesses.

Also Read: How to Use Translator in Bing

Now that you have learned what Bing Rewards, we hope your doubts are cleared with the methods shown in this guide. Keep visiting TechCult to know the latest tech walkarounds. If you have any queries or suggestions, do reach out to us in the comment section.

title: How to Get Rid of Facebook Marketplace Limit Reached Problem
subtitle: How to Get Rid of Facebook Marketplace Limit Reached Problem: Use Facebook often, Engage With Other Listings & Finish Your Facebook Profile
author: Techcult
summary: How to Get Rid of Facebook Marketplace Limit Reached Problem: Use Facebook often, Engage With Other Listings & Finish Your Facebook Profile
content:
Facebook is not just a platform for posting, sharing memes, or connecting with friends and family; it is also a full-blown place to buy and sell products. With over a billion monthly active users in Marketplace, it has become a globally known community of businessmen. If you have attempted to sell your items there, you have most likely seen the Limit Reached notice. This can cause upend your listing strategies, therefore you should know how to get rid of the Facebook Marketplace Limit Reached problem. Let’s jump right in!

  • How to Get Rid of Facebook Marketplace Limit Reached Problem
  • Method 1: Use Facebook Frequently
  • Method 2: Engage With Other Listings
  • Method 3: List Products Slowly
  • Method 4: Finish Your Facebook Profile
  • Method 5: Report a Problem
  • Method 6: Clear Facebook Cache
  • Method 7: Turn Off VPN

How to Get Rid of Facebook Marketplace Limit Reached Problem

The Facebook Marketplace Limit Reached issue might make you cut your sales even before you have fully started. Keep reading to find all the possible solutions.

Method 1: Use Facebook Frequently

In order to begin selling goods on Marketplace, you must establish credibility with Facebook. This means that users should be more active on the platform. How to do that? Message people, share images and videos on the network, like and comment on your friends’ postings, and more. Facebook’s algorithm can also identify your account as active and authentic if you play a few games, follow a few sites, or post a few personal updates.

Method 2: Engage With Other Listings

Another common strategy to make your profile feel more human is by engaging with listings in the Facebook Marketplace. This includes joining other community groups. Group listings, according to some users, are less restrictive, allowing you to continue selling in your neighborhood while you wait for the primary Marketplace limitations to relax.

Method 3: List Products Slowly

If you list products very frequently, then chances are that Facebook recognizes your account as a bot and limits your listing capacity. To avoid this, list products one at a time and take a day or two to post.

Method 4: Finish Your Facebook Profile

Convincing Facebook that you are not a fraudulent seller or a robot can also be achieved by completing your profile. For example, adding a profile picture, and banner, and providing some personal information.

Method 5: Report a Problem

If nothing is working out for you, then the best way to remove the Facebook Marketplace listing limit is by reaching out to their team. Here’s how you can do the same:

  1. Open Facebook and tap on the hamburger icon at the bottom right ribbon.
  2. Swipe down and tap on Help & Support.
  3. Now, select Report a Problem.
  4. Tap on Continue to Report.
  5. Select Include.
  6. Swipe down and select Marketplace under Choose Feature.
  7. Type in your issue under the What went wrong? Text box.
  8. Select between Take screenshot, Record screen, or Upload from phone.
  9. Then, tap on Send.

Your report will go for review and a possible solution should be sent to you.

Method 6: Clear Facebook Cache

If you haven’t cleared the Facebook app cache in some time then chances are the high storage cache may cause the app to glitch. Follow the steps to remove it:

Note: Not all Android devices have the same interface since they vary from manufacturer to manufacturer. Hence, ensure the correct settings have been selected according to your device’s language. 

  1. Open Settings and tap on Apps.
  2. Swipe down and tap on Facebook
  3. Tap on Storage & cache.
  4. Then, select Clear cache.

You can reopen Facebook and check if your problem is fixed.

Method 7: Turn Off VPN

When you connect to a VPN network, Facebook may detect an unknown IP address and impose a limit on your account. You should disable the VPN, restart Facebook, and try your luck with Marketplace again.

Also Read: What Is Facebook Take a Break Feature and How to Use it?

By following the methods shown in this guide, we hope that now you know how to get rid of the Facebook Marketplace limit reached problem. Do not hesitate to drop a comment or suggestions in case you have any queries. Keep visiting TechCult to learn more tech-related walkarounds.

title: What Is Facebook Take a Break Feature and How to Use it?
subtitle: What Is Facebook Take a Break Feature and How to Use it: Visit user's profile, Tap on Friends, Select Take a break, Select your options
author: Techcult
summary: What Is Facebook Take a Break Feature and How to Use it: Visit user's profile, Tap on Friends, Select Take a break, Select your options
content:
With over 3 billion monthly active users, Facebook has always been regarded as the first example of a social media platform. You can connect with your friends and family and get a look at their current lives. While it is amazing to stay in touch with so many people, sometimes we may wish to control what comes on our feed. So, if you are wondering what is Facebook take a break feature and how to use it, you’re at the right place! Keep reading!

  • What Is Facebook Take a Break Feature and How to Use it?
  • How to Use Take a Break from Someone on Facebook
  • Method 1: Via Mobile
  • Method 2: Via Desktop

What Is Facebook Take a Break Feature and How to Use it?

The Take a Break feature lets users see less of someone’s posts on their feed without blocking or restricting them. It is a great way to catch a break from users you have grown over but don’t want to unfriend. By using this, Facebook will no longer show you any posts related to the selected users.

How to Use Take a Break from Someone on Facebook

You can easily use this feature on Facebook.

Method 1: Via Mobile

Follow the steps to do the same from the Facebook app on your smartphone:

  1. Open Facebook and tap on the search icon from the top ribbon.
  2. Type in the name of the friend and select their profile.
  3. Tap on Friends.
  4. Then, select Take a break.
  5. Tap on See options under See less of [user] profile.
  6. Select between See [user] anywhere on Facebook or Limit where you see [user].
  7. Now, select Save.
  8. Then, tap on See options under Limit what [user] can see.
  9. Select between Keep current privacy settings or Hide your posts from [user].
  10. Select Save.
  11. Lastly, tap on See options under Edit who can see past posts.
  12. Select between Keep all posts as they are, Edit individual posts, and Edit all my posts and posts I’m tagged in.
  13. Tap on Done once you have edited your posts.

Now you will stop seeing the user on your Facebook timeline.

Method 2: Via Desktop

The desktop version of Facebook automatically offers users a separate website to add friends they wish to take a break from. Here’s how you can use it:

  1. Visit the official Take a Break website on Facebook.
  2. Type in the username under the Take a break search box.
  3. Follow steps 5-12 mentioned under Method 1: Via Mobile.
  4. Then, click on Done.

You will successfully restrict the user.

We hope now you can easily figure out what is Facebook Take a Break feature and how to use it after following the methods outlined in this guide. Keep catching up with TechCult for more such new tech-related walkarounds. If you have any suggestions or queries, do reach out to us in the comment section.

title: How to Schedule Reels on Facebook
subtitle: How to Schedule Reels on Facebook: Click on the Meta Business Suite, Click on Create reel then click on Add Video, Click on Next, Click on the Schedule
author: Techcult
summary: How to Schedule Reels on Facebook: Click on the Meta Business Suite, Click on Create reel then click on Add Video, Click on Next, Click on the Schedul...
content:
For reaching a larger audience on Facebook it is essential to schedule reel at the time when your followers are most active. It helps you strategically plan out what and when to post so you can focus on creating engaging content and ensure that your page remains active and consistent even if you are not constantly online. In this comprehensive guide, we’ll help you learn how to schedule reels on Facebook.

  • How to Schedule Reels on Facebook
  • Method 1: Using Meta Business Suite
  • Method 2: Using Planner
  • How Can I Reschedule a Facebook Reel that I’ve Already Scheduled
  • What Are the Benefits of Scheduling Facebook Reel?
  • What Are the Tips for Scheduling Facebook Reels?

How to Schedule Reels on Facebook

Currently scheduling a reel directly through your Facebook account is not possible. To schedule a reel, you will need to log in to your meta business suite.

Follow the steps given below to do so:

Method 1: Using Meta Business Suite

  1. Open your desktop browser and visit the Facebook login page.
  2. Log in to your Facebook account then switch to your page.
  3. Click on the Meta Business Suite option from the bottom left corner.
  4. Click on Create reel then click on Add Video and select the reel video you want to share.
  5. Click on Next from the bottom right corner.
  6. Click on Add audio if needed. Once done, click on Next again.
  7. From the Scheduling options click on Schedule then select your desired date and time.
  8. Click on the Schedule button from the bottom right corner.

Method 2: Using Planner

  1. Follow steps 1-3 from the previous method. Next, click on Planner located in the left corner.
  2. From the calendar Select the date you want your reel to be published.
  3. Now, start creating a reel, click on either the Add video or Add photo option.
  4. Select the content you want to share as a reel. Next, click on Next,
  5. If necessary, crop, trim, or add text and audio to your reel then click on Next.
  6. Click on Schedule then choose your desired date and time.
  7. Lastly, click on Schedule.

How Can I Reschedule a Facebook Reel that I’ve Already Scheduled

You can reschedule a Facebook reel that you’ve already scheduled just by following these given steps:

  1. Navigate to your Meta Business Suite home page.
  2. Click on Posts & reels then navigate to the Scheduled section.
  3. From the available scheduled posts select the reel you want to edit.
  4. Click on the three-dots icon given next to the selected reel.
  5. Select the Reschedule reel option.
  6. Click on date and time and re-enter the date and time you want to schedule.
  7. Once done, click on the Reschedule button.

What Are the Benefits of Scheduling Facebook Reel?

There are numerous benefits of scheduling Facebook reels some include:

  • Consistency: Scheduling ensures a steady flow of content, even during your busiest periods.
  • Time efficiency: By scheduling reels in advance, you can save hours that can be used for other important tasks.
  • Boost engagement: By uploading reels during peak engagement periods, you can maximize the visibility of your reel and reach a larger audience.
  • Grow your audience: Reels have the potential to show up on different parts of Facebook. By scheduling reels you can target different demographic audiences in various time zones.

content:

How to Use Grok AI for Free on Twitter/X

Grok is free to use for all Twitter users, no matter their subscription. You can use it with just a few simple steps.

Method 1: Via Phone

You can easily find Grok from the Twitter app on your smartphone. Here’s how:

  1. Open Twitter and tap on GROK from the bottom ribbon.
  2. Type in your prompt under the Ask anything box.
  3. Tap on the arrow icon to send.
  4. Tap on DeepSearch to get detailed answers.
  5. Select Think to get answers on match or coding.
  6. Tap on the pin icon from the message box.
  7. Select Photos, Files, or Camera to insert external information from your phone.
  8. Tap on the microphone icon to use your voice for commands.
  9. Tap on the timer icon at the top right corner to view history.
  10. Select the new icon at the top right corner to start a new conversation.

Now you can use Grok anytime.

Method 2: Via Desktop

You can also do the same from the web version of Twitter. Check out the steps below:

  1. Log in to Twitter and click on Grok from the left menu.
  2. Type in your prompt under the Ask anything box.
  3. Tap on the arrow icon to send.
  4. Tap on DeepSearch to get detailed answers.
  5. Select Think to get answers on match or coding.
  6. Click on the Attach from the message box.
  7. Select an image or file from your PC and click on Open.

This way, you can easily use Grok to ask questions or create images.

title: How to Copy or Share Twitter Profile and Tweet Link Using Any Device
subtitle: How to Copy or Share Twitter Profile and Tweet Link Using Any Device: Select Profile, Tap on share icon, Select Copy Link to Profile
author: Techcult
summary: How to Copy or Share Twitter Profile and Tweet Link Using Any Device: Select Profile, Tap on share icon, Select Copy Link to Profile
content:
Twitter (X) is used for not only connecting with people but sharing viral memes, breaking news, and useful content. Knowing how to copy or share a Twitter profile and tweet link using any device ensures you can quickly send important posts to friends, save useful content, or even reference tweets later. This feature comes in handy for sharing breaking news, viral moments, or even your profile across different platforms. So, what are you waiting for? Let’s get right into it!

  • How to Copy or Share Twitter Profile and Tweet Link Using Any Device
  • Method 1: Sharing Own Profile Link
  • Method 2: Sharing User’s Profile Link
  • Method 3: Sharing Tweet Link

How to Copy or Share Twitter Profile and Tweet Link Using Any Device

Twitter makes it easy to share content, whether it’s a profile you admire or a tweet worth spreading. Whether you’re using a phone or a computer, having quick access to these links helps keep the conversation going beyond the platform.

Method 1: Sharing Own Profile Link

You can easily access a profile link on Twitter.

Option 1: Via Phone

Here’s how you can get your profile link and share it with others from your smartphone:

  1. Open Twitter and tap on the home icon from the bottom left ribbon.
  2. Tap on your profile picture at the top left corner.
  3. Select Profile.
  4. Now, tap on the share icon at the top right corner.
  5. Then, tap on Copy Link to Profile. Please note that this option can also be named as Share link for some smartphones.

This way you can quickly send your Twitter profile link.

Option 2: Via Desktop

Let’s check out how to do so from the web version of Twitter:

  1. Log in to Twitter and click on Profile from the left menu.
  2. Double-click on the URL from the browser’s address bar at the top of the screen.
  3. Press ctrl and C to copy the link.

This way you can get the link to your profile.

Method 2: Sharing User’s Profile Link

Similarly, you can also do the same for other users’ profiles:

  1. Open Twitter and select the user of your choice.
  2. Tap on the three dots at the top right corner.
  3. Then, tap on Share [user] via. . .
  4. Select Copy Link to Profile.

This way you can get the profile link of any Twitter user.

Option 2: Via Desktop

In the same way, you can also get someone else’s URL from your PC:

  1. Log in to Twitter and select the user.
  2. Click on the three dots beside their profile picture.
  3. Now, select Share [user] via. . .
  4. Then, click on the copy link icon under Share link. Please note that you can also copy the URL from the address bar.

Your link will be successfully copied and ready to be shared.

Method 3: Sharing Tweet Link

You can share tweet links that direct the person to the post, saving time and effort. This is how to do so:

  1. Open Twitter and select the tweet of your choice.
  2. Tap on the share icon at the bottom right corner of the tweet.
  3. Then, select Copy link.

Now you can easily share the tweet link with other people.

Option 2: Via Desktop

Lastly, here’s how you can use your PC to copy tweet links:

  1. Log in to Twitter and select your tweet.
  2. Click on the share icon under the tweet.
  3. Then, select Copy link. Please note that you can also copy the URL from the address bar.

You will be share to share any tweets.

Also Read: How to Check Who Blocked You on Twitter

Now that you have seen how to copy or share a Twitter profile and tweet link using any device, we hope your doubts are cleared with the methods shown in this guide. For more helpful tips and tricks, stay tuned, and feel free to share your suggestions in the comments below.

title: Fix Apps Drawer Icon Missing Issue in Samsung Devices
subtitle: Fix Apps Drawer Icon Missing Issue in Samsung Devices: Power off your device for a couple of minutes and turn it back on
author: Techcult
summary: Fix Apps Drawer Icon Missing Issue in Samsung Devices: Power off your device for a couple of minutes and turn it back on
content:
The app drawer is a very important part of our Android phones, where we can quickly access any installed apps. Arranged in alphabetical order, you can easily find apps that are not present on your home screen. Naturally, it can be pretty frustrating when you go to open it and find the feature missing from your phone. This leads to finding any issue to fix for the apps drawer icon missing in Samsung devices. Don’t worry, today we bring you all the solutions in this guide!

  • Fix Apps Drawer Icon Missing Issue in Samsung Devices
  • Method 1: Restart Phone
  • Method 2: Enable App Drawer
  • Method 3: Reset Your Launcher
  • Method 4: Default Launcher

Fix Apps Drawer Icon Missing Issue in Samsung Devices

With these fixes, you will be able to get back to your phone working the normal way as soon as possible.

Method 1: Restart Phone

Sometimes an internal glitch can cause icons to stop showing up on phones. Simply, power off your device for a couple of minutes and turn it back on to see if this minor issue is resolved.

Method 2: Enable App Drawer

Sometimes, the app drawer feature is automatically disabled in many phones. Therefore, enabling it will get the icon to show up.

Note: Not all Android devices have the same interface since they vary from manufacturer to manufacturer. Hence, ensure the correct settings have been selected according to your device’s language. 

Option 1A: Via Settings

Some layouts don’t have an app drawer interface. Follow the steps below to enable it:

  1. Open Settings and tap on Home screen & Lock screen.
  2. Tap on Home screen.
  3. Now, select With drawer.
  4. Then, tap on Apply.
  5. Select Switch.

The app drawer will be available to use.

Option 2B: Via Settings

You can also do the same from your main settings:

  1. Open Settings and tap on Home Screen or Launcher.
  2. Find the App Drawer or App Tray option.
  3. Turn the toggle on for App Drawer or App Tray. Please note that if this option is not available, then tap on the search icon, enter App Drawer or App Tray, and select the option.

Your problem should be solved.

Method 3: Reset Your Launcher

Resetting your launcher to its default settings will clear out any settings to disable the app drawer.

  1. Open the Settings app and select Apps.
  2. Select your launcher app, e.g., Google Now Launcher, One UI Home, Samsung Experience Home, or much more.
  3. Tap on Clear Data and Clear Cache.

Restart your phone and check whether you can access the app drawer again.

Method 4: Default Launcher

If you are using a third-party or custom launcher, then chances are it does not support the app drawer icon.

  1. Open Settings and tap on Home Screen or Launcher.
  2. Tap on Default Launcher or System Launcher.
  3. Select the launcher of your choice.

Restart your phone and check if the app drawer is back again.

Also Read: How to Access the App Drawer on Android 10

Now you will no longer have a difficult time figuring out how fix for the apps drawer icon missing issue in Samsung devices after following this guide. For more helpful tips and tricks, stay tuned, and feel free to share your suggestions in the comments below.

title: How to Access the App Drawer on Android 10

author: Techcult
summary: How to Access the App Drawer on Android 10: You can get the app drawer by simply swiping up from your home screen
content:
The new Android 10 brought significant design changes and feature updates to our mobile operating system. From new gestures to dark mode, people are learning all about the new interface. One surprisingly common question that trips people up is how to access the app drawer on their Android 10. You’ve got apps installed but can’t figure out where they all went, or the gesture that used to work suddenly does nothing? Don’t worry, here’s all you need to know!

  • How to Access the App Drawer on Android 10
  • Method 1: Swipe Up on Home Screen
  • Method 2: Swipe Right or Left on Home Screen
  • Method 3: Via Search Option
  • What is App Drawer in Android?
  • Does Android 12 Have an App Drawer?

How to Access the App Drawer on Android 10

Let reaching your app drawer become second nature again.

Note: Not all Android devices have the same interface since they vary from manufacturer to manufacturer. Hence, ensure the correct settings have been selected according to your device’s language. 

Method 1: Swipe Up on Home Screen

You can get the app drawer by simply swiping up from your home screen. All downloaded apps will be visible once the drawer opens.

Method 2: Swipe Right or Left on Home Screen

While some Android phones open app drawers when you swipe either right or left on your home screen.

Method 3: Via Search Option

If you are unable to access the app drawer from your home screen, open the search feature and type ‘apps’ or ‘app drawer’. This way, you will be able to see all the installed apps at once.

What is App Drawer in Android?

App Drawer on Android is a place where you can see and launch all of your installed apps. All apps are laid out in alphabetical order, making it pretty easy to find your desired app. You can even drag apps from the drawer and drop them on your home screen, creating a shortcut for quick access.

Does Android 12 Have an App Drawer?

Yes, Android 12 also has the App Drawer feature on all phones.

How to Update Android Apps Automatically

If you want a sure-shot way to guarantee the optimum performance of your apps, then it’s beneficial to keep them up-to-date. Today we will show you different ways to do the same.

  1. Open Google Play Store and tap on your profile at the top right corner.
  2. Tap on Manage apps & devices.

This way only your chosen apps will get updated on an Android smartphone.

This way you can successfully turn off auto-updates on your phone.

title: How to Do a Hard Reset on Android
subtitle: How to Do a Hard Reset on Android: Hold down the side power & volume down buttons, Release the power button once the phone’s logo is visible
author: Techcult
summary: How to Do a Hard Reset on Android: Hold down the side power & volume down buttons, Release the power button once the phone’s logo is visible
content:
Android devices are used in the houses of billions of consumers worldwide. But even as the most popular operating system, it is adept to slowdowns or unresponsiveness. If you’re sick of using Band-Aid solutions and your phone isn’t working smoothly anymore, or if it keeps freezing, you might want to know how to do a hard reset on your Android phone. Well, the wait is over, let’s jump right in!

  • How to Do a Hard Reset on Android
  • Method 1: Via Force Restart
  • Method 2: Via System Settings
  • Method 2: Via Recovery Mode

How to Do a Hard Reset on Android

By performing a hard reset, users can return their phones to their factory settings just like their initial condition. Before you start, keep in mind that your phone will lose all its saved data and information.

Note: Since not all Android devices have the same interface, they vary from manufacturer to manufacturer. Hence, ensure the correct settings have been selected according to your device’s language. 

Method 1: Via Force Restart

The easiest way to reset your smartphone is through the force-start method. Here’s what you need to do:

    1. Hold down the side power button. Please note that on many smartphones users may also need to simultaneously hold the volume down button.
    2. Release the power button once the phone’s logo is visible on the screen.

This way your phone will open fully reset.

Method 2: Via System Settings

You can access your phone’s settings to do the same. Here’s how:

  1. Open Settings and tap on General Management.
  2. Swipe down and tap on Reset. Please note that on some devices users may get this option under Advanced Settings.
  3. Now, select Factory data reset.
  4. Swipe down and select RESET DEVICE from the confirmation prompt.
  5. Type in your phone’s security pin if prompted.
  6. Now, tap on DELETE ALL.

This way your phone will go into a hard reset.

Method 2: Via Recovery Mode

You can also use the recovery mode and force restart your Android mobile into a hard reset. Follow the steps mentioned below:

  1. Press the power button to shut down your smartphone.
  2. Press the power button and the volume up button simultaneously. Please note that with some devices, users need to plug their phones into a computer while it’s turned off to get this option.
  3. Press the volume down button and go over the Wipe data/factory reset option.
  4. Press the Power button to select the option.

Your phone will now be reset.

We hope now you can easily figure out how to do a hard reset on your Android phone by following the methods outlined in this guide. Do not hesitate to reach out to us in the comment section. Keep visiting TechCult for more tech-related know-hows.

title: How to Turn Off MMS on Android
subtitle: How to Turn Off MMS on Android: Tap on Message Settings, Select Advanced, Turn the toggle off for Auto-download MMS
author: Techcult
summary: How to Turn Off MMS on Android: Tap on Message Settings, Select Advanced, Turn the toggle off for Auto-download MMS
content:
Multimedia Messaging Service (MMS) lets you send and receive messages on your Android device that have photos, videos, audio files, and other types of multimedia material. MMS can be helpful, but there are times when you might want to turn it off, like when you want to save money on data, stop media from downloading automatically, or fix problems with messages. There are several ways to turn off MMS on your Android phone or tablet, which we will explain to you in this guide.

  • How to Turn Off MMS on Android
  • Method 1: Disable Auto-Retrieve for Multimedia Messages
  • Method 2: Use a Third-Party Messaging App

How to Turn Off MMS on Android

You can easily turn off MMS on Android using the different methods mentioned below:

Method 1: Disable Auto-Retrieve for Multimedia Messages

Follow the steps mentioned below to disable auto-retrieve for multimedia messages:

  1. Open the Messages app on your Android device.
  2. Tap on your profile at the top-right corner.
  3. Tap on Message Settings.
  4. Swipe down and tap on Advanced.
  5. Turn the toggle off for Auto-download MMS.

After turning this setting off, your device will not download any MMS messages with pictures or videos. 

Method 2: Use a Third-Party Messaging App

There are many third-party apps like QKSMS, Pulse SMS, Textra SMS, and Signal. Many of these apps allow you to completely turn off MMS functionality.

Note: We do not endorse the use of third-party apps as they may expose your device to unwanted malware or viruses. User discretion is advised!  

  1. Install the Signal app from the Google Play Store.
  2. Grant all the permissions asked and set up your account.
  3. Tap on the three dots in the top right corner.
  4. Tap on Settings.
  5. Select Data and storage.
  6. Tap on Media auto-download section.
  7. Tap on When using mobile data.
  8. Uncheck all the boxes and tap on OK.
  9. Tap on When using Wi-Fi.
  10. Uncheck all the boxes and tap on OK.
  11. Select Roaming.
  12. Uncheck all the boxes and tap on OK. 

Now, no data will be downloaded on your device.

Also Read: 12 Best MMS Apps for Android

Remember that turning off MMS means you won’t be able to send or receive multimedia texts with pictures, videos, and other files. For now, if you still want to share media with your friends, you’ll have to use email or messaging apps like WhatsApp.If you have any queries or suggestions do let us know in the comments section below. Stay tuned to Techcult for more such helpful guides.
