title: How to Fix SOS Only on an iPhone
subtitle: How to Fix SOS Only on an iPhone: Press and release the volume up button.Press and release the volume down button.Long-press the power button
author: Techcult
summary: How to Fix SOS Only on an iPhone: Press and release the volume up button.Press and release the volume down button.Long-press the power button
content:
iPhones are known for their reliable cellular connectivity and uninterrupted network. But sometimes users have noticed their phones getting the SOS or SOS Only status, which stops them from making calls or sending messages. This is when you urgently need to know how to fix SOS only on an iPhone before missing important calls or getting stranded without communication. So, let’s jump right in!

  • How to Fix SOS Only on an iPhone
  • Method 1: Enable Airplane Mode
  • Method 2: Force Stop iPhone
  • Method 3: Update Carrier Settings
  • Method 4: Reinsert SIM Card
  • Method 5: Turn on Data Roaming
  • Method 6: Reset Network Settings
  • Method 7: Update Software
  • Method 8: Contact Carrier Provider

How to Fix SOS Only on an iPhone

Now you don’t have to be annoyed with the constant SOS alert on your notification bar.

Method 1: Enable Airplane Mode

The easiest way to resolve this issue is to quickly enable airplane mode for 15 seconds and then disable it. Doing this will refresh your network back to your cellular data.

Method 2: Force Stop iPhone

Force restarting your phone will also help remove the SOS sign.

  1. Press and release the volume up button.
  2. Press and release the volume down button.
  3. Long-press the power button until the screen shuts down and restarts.

This will restart your phone.

Method 3: Update Carrier Settings

Updating your carrier settings to their latest version will also help recognise your iPhone:

  1. Open Settings and tap on General.
  2. Tap on About.
  3. Wait for a few seconds for a carrier settings update pop-up if you are eligible for it.
  4. Then, select Update.

After your carrier settings are updated, you should no longer get the SOS alert.

Method 4: Reinsert SIM Card

If you have a physical SIM card, then remove it from your phone. Wait for a few seconds and insert it back on to check if your issue is resolved.

Method 5: Turn on Data Roaming

If you have been travelling and noticing the alert, chances are that you have not enabled roaming on your iPhone.

  1. Open Settings and tap on Mobile Service.
  2. Select Mobile Data Options.
  3. Now, turn the toggle on for Data Roaming.

This way, you can use your carrier outside of your country.

Method 6: Reset Network Settings

If none of the methods are working, it may be time to reset your network settings back to default:

  1. Open Settings and tap on General.
  2. Scroll down and tap on Transfer or Reset iPhone.
  3. Select Reset.
  4. Then, tap on Reset Network Settings.
  5. Follow the on-screen instructions.

Your settings will be successfully reset.

Method 7: Update Software

You can also update your iPhone to its latest version.

  1. Open Settings and tap on General.
  2. Tap on Software Update.
  3. Then, tap on Update Now.

After your phone is updated, check if your problem is fixed.

Method 8: Contact Carrier Provider

If no other fix is working, then it is best to contact your carrier provider and ask the expert to solve your issue.

Also Read: How to Turn Off Flashlight on iPhone

Now you will no longer have a difficult time figuring how to fix SOS only on an iPhone after following this guide. For more helpful tips and tricks, stay tuned, and feel free to share your suggestions in the comments below.

title: Shortcut for Undo and Redo
subtitle: Shortcut for Undo and Redo: Press Ctrl and Z keys to undo, Press Ctrl and Y keys to redo. In Mac press Cmd + Z to undo & Cmd+Shift+Z to redo
author: Techcult
summary: Shortcut for Undo and Redo: Press Ctrl and Z keys to undo, Press Ctrl and Y keys to redo. In Mac press Cmd + Z to undo & Cmd+Shift+Z to redo
content:
Whether you’re a professional writer, editor, or Excel user, you know how important basic shortcuts are. They speed up your work and minimize extra effort, making it easy to for any kind of typing work. If you’re having a hard time knowing the basic shortcut for undo and redo, then today is your day! Let’s get started.

  • Shortcut for Undo and Redo
  • Why Use the Redo Undo Keyboard Shortcut?
  • Undo and Redo in Excel and Word
  • How Many Steps Can You Undo?
  • Other Ways to Undo or Redo Without Shortcuts
  • Troubleshooting Undo/Redo Problems
  • How to Undo and Redo in Other Apps

Shortcut for Undo and Redo

For Windows or Linux PC, simply press the Ctrl and Z keys together to undo and the Ctrl and Y keys to redo, respectively. If you are a Mac user, then press the Cmd + Z to undo and Command + Shift + Z to redo over any document or Excel sheet.

Why Use the Redo Undo Keyboard Shortcut?

Using the shortcut keys for redo and undo ensures a smooth flow of work. You are able to fix your mistakes and type quickly without using the backspace button on your documents.

Undo and Redo in Excel and Word

The undo and redo shortcuts for both Word and Excel are the same as stated above.

How Many Steps Can You Undo?

Users are allowed to undo over 100 times in a document.

Other Ways to Undo or Redo Without Shortcuts

You can also use the Backspace and Delete buttons or the mouse to do the same. Word and Excel also have the undo and redo buttons on their platform.

  1. Type anything in a document or enter your input in Excel.
  2. Click on the left arrow icon at the top left corner to undo.
  3. Then, click on the right arrow icon at the top left corner to redo.

This way, you can easily undo or redo.

Troubleshooting Undo/Redo Problems

If your shortcuts are not working, try these tips:

  • Close the program and re-open.
  • Check if undo or redo options are available to be used.
  • Restart your desktop.

How to Undo and Redo in Other Apps

The same shortcut combinations are also used in other platforms, like:

  • Google Docs: Ctrl + Z for Undo and Ctrl + Y or Redo on Windows. Command + Z and Command + Shift + Z on Mac for undo and redo, respectively.
  • Outlook: Undo typing in emails with the same keys.
  • PowerPoint: Ctrl + Z and Ctrl + Y on Windows. Command + Z and Command + Shift + Z on Mac.
  • Apple Pages: Command + Z for undo, Command + Shift + Z for redo.

title: How to Turn Off Flashlight on iPhone
subtitle: How to Turn Off Flashlight on iPhone: Press the power button to lock your phone. Now, tap on the flashlight icon
author: Techcult
summary: How to Turn Off Flashlight on iPhone: Press the power button to lock your phone. Now, tap on the flashlight icon
content:
Whether you’re looking for something in the dark or finding your keys under the couch, our phones’ torches go a long way to help us. Apple made it super easy to turn on with a quick swipe and or a few taps. But sometimes that flashlight gets stuck on, keeps turning on accidentally in your pocket, or you simply can’t figure out how to make it stop shining when you’re done with it. This is when knowing how to turn off the flashlight on iPhone is the need of the hour. So, let’s show you how it’s done.

  • How to Turn Off Flashlight on iPhone
  • Method 1: Via Lock Screen
  • Method 2: Via Siri 
  • Method 3: Via Control Center
  • Method 4: Via Action Button

How to Turn Off Flashlight on iPhone

You can choose various ways to disable your flashlight:

Method 1: Via Lock Screen

You can easily turn off the flashlight right from your screen:

  1. Press the power button to lock your phone.
  2. Now, tap on the flashlight icon at the bottom left corner.

The flashlight will be disabled.

Method 2: Via Siri 

You can also use the voice assistant Siri to do the same. Simply say “Hey Siri, turn off the flashlight” to make it work.

Method 3: Via Control Center

Control Center also has a flashlight button to turn it off or on.

  1. Swipe the screen from the top right corner.
  2. Tap on the flashlight icon.
  3. Hold the screen and drag it down to the lowest light.

This way, you can control the flashlight.

Method 4: Via Action Button

If you use iPhone 15 or later, you can also assign flashlight to your action button and use it to turn it on or off.

  1. Open Settings and tap on Action Button.
  2. Swipe and choose flashlight.
  3. Click on the action button on iPhone to turn on and click again to turn off.

This is a quick way to use your flashlight.

Now you will no longer have a difficult time figuring out how to turn off the flashlight on iPhone after following this guide. For more helpful tips and tricks, stay tuned, and feel free to share your suggestions in the comments below.

content:
Android emulators play a huge role in making your desktop an even better version of itself. They can transform and give access to any apps available on your phones. But with so many fake sites and malware concerns, one has to wonder what the current best safe Android emulator for Windows is. Don’t worry, today you will get all your answers!

  • Best Android Emulator for Windows (2026)
  • 1. NoxPlayer
  • 2. Prime OS

  • 4. Bliss OS

Best Android Emulator for Windows (2026)

Now turn your computer into an Android phone with these top software.

1. NoxPlayer

NoxPlayer strikes a balance between gaming performance and everyday Android app use on your PC. It brings multi-instance support, macro recording, gamepad and keyboard controls, plus customizable setups that work across a wide range of apps and games. You get virtual location tools and advanced button mapping too. While benchmarks sometimes show it lagging behind BlueStacks or LDPlayer, users stick with it for the easy customization and solid all-around flexibility.

2. Prime OS

Prime OS skips traditional emulation by running as a full Android-based operating system you install on your PC through dual boot or USB. That setup delivers native Android performance without any overhead, perfect for gaming or productivity tasks. You get true OS-level speed that feels built right into your machine.

3. Genymotion

Genymotion targets developers with cloud-based Android machines and strong testing features for QA teams or CI/CD pipelines. Configure multiple virtual devices picking Android versions, screen sizes, and sensors as needed. Pricing leans business-oriented and setup takes some work, but the scalability beats local emulators for serious development work.

4. Bliss OS

Bliss OS transforms your PC into a customizable Android operating system you boot from USB or install alongside Windows. It gives you deep control over the Android environment for testing, development, or custom workflows. Performance depends on your hardware and install method, but the freedom to tweak everything stands out big time.

5. BlueStacks

BlueStacks tops most “best Android emulator” lists thanks to its powerful performance on Windows and macOS with Google Play Store access plus APK support. It runs Android apps and games smoothly while offering key mapping, multi-instance running, and eco mode to cut resource use. Casual users and hardcore gamers both find what they need here.

6. LDPlayer

LDPlayer focuses on raw gaming speed, offering one of the fastest Android emulators with high frame rates up to 240 FPS with interpolation. Keyboard, controller mapping, and macro tools shine in demanding titles like PUBG Mobile or Free Fire. It runs well even on mid-range systems, which keeps competitive gamers coming back.

7. MEmu Play

MEmu Play holds up strong as an Android emulator for Windows with solid support for both AMD and Intel chips. It handles apps and games equally well through an intuitive interface that feels smooth right away. Frame interpolation delivers real results. I tested Free Fire at native 60 FPS and bumped it to 120 FPS with interpolation on. The smoothness jumps out immediately with no extra input lag.

8. GameLoop

GameLoop serves as the official Android emulator for gaming hits like PUBG and Call of Duty Mobile, built straight by Tencent. It packs a special anti-cheat system to keep matches fair across the board. Speeds crush it for those specific titles, giving you the smoothest experience with guaranteed compatibility. Stick to these games and you won’t find better.

9. Droid4x

Droid4X turns Windows PCs into Android hubs for mobile apps and games from XP to 10. It handles most Play Store titles like Clash of Clans or Subway Surfers with custom controls and direct app downloads. Runs on Android 4.2 or above and just needs 2GB RAM to crank your PC into a gaming beast.

10. ARChon

ARChon keeps things ultra-lightweight by running Android apps right inside the Google Chrome browser without any heavy installs. Load unpacked APKs converted through the chromeos-apk CLI and you’re good to go. Limited to Android 7 APIs without hardware acceleration, but it works great on locked-down IT laptops where software installs get blocked.

11. Ko Player

Ko Player ranks high for Windows 7 and up, especially running games like Call of Duty or Subway Surfers smoothly. Plug in gamepads, keyboards, or other peripherals for full immersion. It only needs a dual-core AMD or Intel CPU with 2GB RAM and runs Android 4 or higher. Match those specs, and you unlock everything without hiccups.

12. Android Studio Emulator

Android Studio Emulator comes straight from Google as the official tool built right into Android Studio for developers testing apps. It lets you try different Android versions and virtual device setups with deep ties to SDK tools. You can mimic screen sizes, OS versions, hardware configs, plus sensors like GPS, accelerometer, and battery levels. Access stays open to the newest Android versions too.

13. Xamarin Android Emulator

Xamarin Android Emulator fits right into Microsoft’s world for pros using Visual Studio. Developers lean on it hard for enterprise AI projects and building heavy-duty apps. Stays your go-to if you’re already in that ecosystem, creating serious stuff.

title: How to Fix Computer Monitor Has a Yellow Tint on Screen
subtitle: Fix Computer Monitor has a Yellow Tint on Screen: Check Hardware Issues, Perform a Power Cycle, and Adjust the Brightness and Contrast
author: Techcult
summary: Fix Computer Monitor has a Yellow Tint on Screen: Check Hardware Issues, Perform a Power Cycle, and Adjust the Brightness and Contrast
content:
Not being able to see colors as organically as possible on your monitor has to be one of the most annoying parts of using a computer. Many people have reported seeing tints on their screens, which make things appear unbalanced and difficult to look at. Since there are numerous reasons why this may occur, today we’ll walk you through every method on how you can fix your computer monitor that has a yellow tint on the screen! Now let’s get started!

  • How to Fix Computer Monitor Has a Yellow Tint on Screen
  • Method 1: Check Hardware Issues
  • Method 2: Perform a Power Cycle
  • Method 3: Adjust the Brightness and Contrast
  • Method 4: Change Color Depth of Monitor
  • Method 5: Adjust White Light
  • Method 6: Update Graphics Display Drivers
  • Method 7: Create New Color Profile Settings
  • Method 8: Adjust Display Calibration
  • Method 9: Remove New Software Installations
  • Method 10: Set Native Refresh Rate and Screen Resolution
  • Method 11: Use System Restore Point

How to Fix Computer Monitor Has a Yellow Tint on Screen

Go back to using your screen just how you got this with these solutions.

Method 1: Check Hardware Issues

Before you take big steps, ensure that your device does not have physical damage on its skin or around the display. If the left side of the Microsoft Surface’s screen is yellow or has yellow patches, that indicates hardware damage.

Method 2: Perform a Power Cycle

Turning off your screen for a while can fix any internal glitches. Shut down your desktop, disconnect the cable wires, and wait for 5-10 minutes. After that, restart the device.

Method 3: Adjust the Brightness and Contrast

A yellow tint can sometimes be caused by uneven brightness or contrast levels on your monitor. Press the brightness button on your keyboard and adjust until colors look more natural.

Method 4: Change Color Depth of Monitor

If your screen shows unusual tints, the color depth setting might be too low. Remember, higher depth like 24-bit or 32-bit usually gives smoother and more accurate colors.

  1. Open Settings and click on Display.
  2. Scroll down and click on Advanced display.
  3. Select Display adapter properties for Display 1 under Display information.
  4. Then, click on Adapter from the top ribbon.
  5. Select the depth of your choice.
  6. Now, click on OK.

This way you can change depth of your desktop.

Method 5: Adjust White Light

Having a night light also sets the screen to warmer tones.

  1. Open Settings and click on System.
  2. Select Display.
  3. Now, turn the toggle on for Night light.

You will get white tones on your screen.

Method 6: Update Graphics Display Drivers

You can also install the latest version of your display driver.

  1. Open Control Panel and click on Device Manager.
  2. Select Display Adapters from the left menu.
  3. Click on the display software.
  4. Then, click on Driver from the top ribbon.
  5. Now, select Update Driver.
  6. Click on OK.

Your problem should be solved.

Method 7: Create New Color Profile Settings

You can also adjust your color profile and add white tones.

  1. Open Control Panel and search for color management.
  2. Click on Color Management.
  3. Select Devices from the top ribbon.
  4. Select the profile under Profiles associated with this device box.
  5. Then, click on Set as Default Profile.

Your screen will be displayed in the select display.

Method 8: Adjust Display Calibration

A very simple reason behind the yellow tint can be a change in the color calibration on your system. Let’s fix that:

  1. Open Control Panel and search for color management.
  2. Click on Color Management.
  3. Select Advanced from the top ribbon.
  4. Then, select Calibrate display under Display Calibration.
  5. Click on How do I calibrate my display? and follow the on-screen instructions.

Check if your screen goes back to normal.

Method 9: Remove New Software Installations

If you have recently installed any new softwares and started facing display issues, chances are that they may be causing the problem.

  1. Press the Windows and R keys together to open the Run dialog.
  2. Type in appwiz.cpl and press Enter.
  3. Right-click on the software of your choice.
  4. Then, select Uninstall.
  5. Click on Yes.

Your issue should be fixed if this is the reason.

Method 10: Set Native Refresh Rate and Screen Resolution

Using the wrong refresh rate or resolution can cause color and display issues on your monitor.

  1. Open Settings > Display > Advanced display.
  2. Click on the Choose a refresh rate box and select your option.

Check if your problem is fixed.

Method 11: Use System Restore Point

If nothing worked, there may have been a change made to the configuration that prevents you from changing it at this time. If you have made a system restore point, you must utilize it in that situation since it will restore your system to a time when the problem did not exist. To finish the process, follow these steps:

  1. Press the Windows and R keys to open Run dialog.
  2. Search rstrui and hit Enter.

Your problem should be solved.

  1. Open Control Panel and search for color management.
  2. Click on Color Management.
  3. Select Devices from the top ribbon.
  4. Select the profile under Profiles associated with this device box.
  5. Then, click on Set as Default Profile.

Your screen will be displayed in the select display.

Method 8: Adjust Display Calibration

A very simple reason behind the yellow tint can be a change in the color calibration on your system. Let’s fix that:

Using the wrong refresh rate or resolution can cause color and display issues on your monitor.

  1. Open Settings > Display > Advanced display.

author: Techcult
summary: How to Get Help in Windows 11: Click on Search from the toolbar, Type in Get Help.Now, select Open, Type in your issue and hit Enter
content:
Microsoft’s Windows 11 is known for its user-friendly features and easy-to-use interface. But we sometimes run into a feature issue or system error that cannot be solved without some help. And what better than to hear the direct advice from the experts? If you want to know how to get help in Windows 11 desktop, your prayers have been answered! Let’s jump right in.

  • How to Get Help in Windows 11
  • Method 1: Via Get Help App
  • Method 2: Via Shortcut Key
  • Method 3: Via Start Tool
  • Method 4: Via Windows 11 Troubleshooters
  • Method 5: Via Settings
  • Method 6: Via Copilot
  • Method 7: Via Microsoft Online Support and Public Forums

How to Get Help in Windows 11

There are several ways you can find answers and tools through the Windows Help feature.

Method 1: Via Get Help App

You can simply access the Get Help feature by searching on your desktop.

  1. Click on Search from the toolbar.
  2. Type in Get Help.
  3. Now, select Open.

That’s it, you can search for your issue.

Method 2: Via Shortcut Key

Your computer has a dedicated shortcut key to open help in different windows. You can press the F1 key across a browser, File Explorer, and Microsoft apps to open help centers directly.

Method 3: Via Start Tool

Some desktops also have a virtual assistant built into their tools. You can click on the start button and type out your question. After you hit Enter, your browser will automatically open with the top results on fixes.

Method 4: Via Windows 11 Troubleshooters

If you have some issues, you can use the Windows 11 troubleshoot option.

  1. Open Settings and click on System from the left menu.
  2. Click on Troubleshoot.
  3. Click on any option that is related to your problem.

Windows will automatically start fixing the issue.

Method 5: Via Settings

You will also find the option in your settings.

  1. Open Settings and click on System from the left menu.
  2. Click on Troubleshoot
  3. Now, select Get help.
  4. Type in your problem and hit Enter.

You will find several articles helping you out.

Method 6: Via Copilot

Microsoft also offers Copilot for quick fixes for any issues:

  1. Click on Search from the toolbar.
  2. Type in Copilot.
  3. Now, select Open.
  4. Type in your issue and hit Enter.

Copilot will start giving you personalised answers.

Method 7: Via Microsoft Online Support and Public Forums

If you are unable to find any related tips regarding your problem, then you can look for external support. Microsoft’s website also offers detailed articles on specific user problems or community forums where anybody can give advice to fix issues. You can also find online communities all across Reddit or Quora where people interact about their problems and solutions in-depth.

subtitle: How to Update Your Lenovo Laptop: Open Settings, Click on Windows Update, Click on Check for Updates, Select Update and download
author: Techcult
summary: How to Update Your Lenovo Laptop: Open Settings, Click on Windows Update, Click on Check for Updates, Select Update and download
content:
Tired of slow runs and decayed functions? It may be time to update your desktop and get back on track. But how do you update your Lenovo laptop and get rid of all the problems? Today, we will show you just that! Without wasting any time, let’s get to it right away.

  • How to Update Your Lenovo Laptop
  • Method 1: Windows Update
  • Method 2: Drivers Update
  • Method 3: Lenovo Vantage Update
  • Method 4: Microsoft Store Update

How to Update Your Lenovo Laptop

With this simple fix, you can upgrade your laptop to all its latest versions.

Method 1: Windows Update

Follow the steps to do the same:

  1. Open Settings and click on Windows Update from the left menu.
  2. Then, click on Check for Updates.
  3. Select Update and download.

Windows will be updated.

Method 2: Drivers Update

If you are looking to upgrade your driver, here’s how you can do so:

  1. Open Control Panel and click on Device Manager.
  2. Select Display Adapters from the left menu.
  3. Click on the display software.
  4. Then, click on Driver from the top ribbon.
  5. Now, select Update Driver.
  6. Click on OK.

Your problem should be solved.

Method 3: Lenovo Vantage Update

You can also update from Vantage:

  1. Open Lenovo Vantage.
  2. Click on the download icon from the left menu.
  3. Click on Check for updates.

Follow the prompts to download and install any available updates for Lenovo applications and drivers.

Method 4: Microsoft Store Update

To update apps, do the steps below mentioned:

  1. Open Microsoft Store and click on Library from the left menu.
  2. Click on Apps.
  3. Select Get Updates.

All apps will be downloaded in their latest versions very easily.

title: How to Check Your Spectrum Email
subtitle: How to Check Your Spectrum Email: Visit Spectrum page, Type in your Email Address and password, Tick on I am not a robot, Click on Sign in
author: Techcult
summary: How to Check Your Spectrum Email: Visit Spectrum page, Type in your Email Address and password, Tick on I am not a robot, Click on Sign in
content:
Spectrum is one of the major internet and cable providers in the US, serving millions of customers with its internet, TV, and phone services. When you sign up for Spectrum internet, you automatically get a free email account that comes with your service package. But here’s where things get confusing. Accessing and checking that email isn’t as easy as you’d expect. You might be wondering where to log in, what your email address even is, or how to check your Spectrum email. Well, we are here to save the day!

  • How to Check Your Spectrum Email
  • Method 1: Via Webmail Site
  • Method 2: Via Mobile App or Email Client
  • Method 3: Old Road Runner or Time Warner Email

How to Check Your Spectrum Email

Spectrum offers multiple ways to access your email, and they don’t always explain which method works best for your situation.

Method 1: Via Webmail Site

The easiest way to get emails is directly through its website:

  1. Visit the official Spectrum page.
  2. Type in your Email Address and password.
  3. Tick on I am not a robot box.
  4. Then, click on Sign in.

That’s it, you will be logged in to your account.

Method 2: Via Mobile App or Email Client

You can manually set up your Spectrum account if you prefer Apple Mail, Outlook, or simply the built-in mail apps on your iPhone or Android device. But there are some settings you’ll need on your smartphone:

Incoming Mail Server (IMAP):

  • Server:mail.twc.com
  • Port:993
  • Security: SSL (make sure SSL/TLS is enabled)

Outgoing Mail Server (SMTP):

  • Server:mail.twc.com
  • Port:587
  • Security: STARTTLS

This setup generally works on most modern devices, but on old or misconfigured apps, you might need to tweak security settings or try different servers like:

  • mail.charter.net
  • mail.brighthouse.com

Method 3: Old Road Runner or Time Warner Email

If you are on an older domain like @rr.com or @twc.com then you need another way to login. But you can follow the same login process at Spectrum as shown in Method 1: Via Webmail Site. Legacy domains work as long as they were not deactivated or merged into a different Spectrum account.

Also Read: What Channel is NBC on Spectrum?

By following the methods shown in this guide, we hope that now you have understood how to check your Spectrum email. Do not hesitate to drop a comment or suggestions in case you have any queries. Keep visiting TechCult to learn more tech-related walkarounds.

title: How to Open Emoji Keyboard on Windows 10/11
subtitle: How to Open Emoji Keyboard on Windows 10/11: Press the Windows and . (period) keys, Click on search or click on emoji icons
author: Techcult
summary: How to Open Emoji Keyboard on Windows 10/11: Press the Windows and . (period) keys, Click on search or click on emoji icons
content:
Don’t let being on a computer stop you from using emojis to express yourself. Thanks to Windows, you have a built-in emoji keyboard that adds fun and flair to your messages. Whether you want to lighten up a chat or social media post, knowing how to quickly open the emoji keyboard on Windows 10 and 11 makes it simple to find the perfect emoji without interrupting your flow. So, let’s get started!

  • How to Open Emoji Keyboard on Windows 10/11
  • Method 1: Via Shortcut Key
  • Method 2: Via Keyboard Emoji Combination
  • Method 3: Via Enabling Touch keyboard

How to Open Emoji Keyboard on Windows 10/11

With just a few clicks, you will be able to make your conversations go from boring to vibrant.

Method 1: Via Shortcut Key

The best way to get the emoji is by using the shortcut key to open the window.

  1. Open the window or app of your choice.
  2. Select the location where you wish to use the emoji.
  3. Now, press the Windows and . (period) keys simultaneously.
  4. Click on the search bar and enter the name of the emoji.
  5. Or, click on the emoji icon from the top ribbon.
  6. Scroll down and select the emoji of your choice.

This way, you can easily use emojis over texts or in a document.

Method 2: Via Keyboard Emoji Combination

There are various key combinations you can use in Microsoft Word or Excel (2019, 2021, 365), that automatically turn them into emojis. This way, you can type emojis on a computer:

  • 🙂 → 😊
  • 🙁 → ☹️
  • 😀 → 😃
  • 😛 → 😛
  • 😉 → 😉
  • 😐 → 😐
  • :-/ → 😕
  • :-* → 😗
  • :-O → 😮
  • :-$ → 🤑
  • :-X → 🤐
  • :-# → 😷
  • :’) → 😂
  • :'( → 😢

Method 3: Via Enabling Touch keyboard

You can also use the on-screen keyboard to always use emojis:

  1. Open Settings and click on Personalisation.
  2. Scroll down and select Taskbar.
  3. Click on Touch keyboard and select Always.
  4. Now, click on the keyboard icon at the bottom right corner of the taskbar.
  5. Select the heart icon at the top left corner.
  6. Then, click on the emoji icon from the top ribbon.
  7. Click on the search bar and enter the name of the emoji.

You can use any emojis in conversations.

Also Read: How to Select All Using Shortcut in Windows 11

Now that you have seen how to open the emoji keyboard, we hope your doubts are cleared with the methods shown in this guide. Keep visiting TechCult to know the latest tech walkarounds. If you have any queries or suggestions, do reach out to us in the comment section.

title: How to Enable 2FA for Fortnite
subtitle: How to Enable 2FA for Fortnite: Login on Epic Games, Click on your profile, Select Account, Click on Password & Security, Select Fortnite 2FA
author: Techcult
summary: How to Enable 2FA for Fortnite: Login on Epic Games, Click on your profile, Select Account, Click on Password & Security, Select Fortnite 2FA
content:
If you play on Fortnite, you know how uncommon and exclusive some skins are, and how much players cherish them. But like any other platform in this digital space, someone can always find a way to get into your account and access these. This is why so many players have started to figure out how to enable 2FA for Fortnite so that they can keep their accounts safe. If you are one of them, this guide will be a great help!

How to Enable 2FA for Fortnite

The good news is that Epic Games has a default option to keep your account extra protected. Let’s see where you can get this setting.

  1. Visit the Epic Games login page and enter your credentials.
  2. Click on your profile at the top right corner.
  3. Select Account.
  4. Click on Password & Security from the menu.
  5. Scroll down and select Fortnite 2FA.
  6. Click on Set up under Epic Authenticator to enable 2FA from the official Epic app.
  7. Click on Set up under Authenticator App to enable 2FA from a third-party authenticator app.
  8. Click on Set up under Email to receive 2FA codes on your registered email.
  9. Click on Set up under SMS to receive 2FA codes on your registered phone number.

After you select your desired option, your two-factor authentication will be enabled.

Rewards for Enabling Fortnite 2FA

Did you know that you not only protect your account but also get rewards for turning on 2FA on Fortnite? The Boogie Down emote is given to players with 2FA. Additionally, the following things will be given to Fortnite users who own the Save the World campaign:

  • 50 Armory Slots
  • 1 Legendary Troll Stash Llama
  • 10 Backpack Slots

Also Read: How to Fix HWID VPN Kick Error in Fortnite

Now that you have seen how to enable 2FA for Fortnite, we hope your doubts are cleared with the methods shown in this guide. Keep visiting TechCult to know the latest tech walkarounds. If you have any queries or suggestions, do reach out to us in the comment section.

Best Free Spelling Bee Games Like NYT

Wordle Unlimited lets you play endless Wordle puzzles all day instead of one locked daily, keeping the letter‑guessing focus like Spelling Bee’s vocab test but guess‑by‑guess. 2. Wordscapes

Wordscapes mixes anagrams, word searches, and crosswords into relaxing brain teasers where you swipe letters to form words against a scenic backdrop. title: 30+ Best Browser Games You Must Play
subtitle: Best Browser Games You Must Play: War Brokers, Skribbl, Slither.io, Slow Roads, NeoPets, RuneScape, Heardle by Spotify, and Akinator

content:
You don’t always need to use your browser for work-related purposes. Some hidden gems can keep you occupied whether you’re viewing movies or streaming games. We’re discussing the best browser games you must play, think everything from puzzles and adventures! So, let’s show you the leading sites right away.

  • Best Browser Games You Must Play in 2025 
  • 1. War Brokers
  • 2. Skribbl
  • 3. Slither.io
  • 4. Slow Roads
  • 5. NeoPets
  • 6. RuneScape
  • 7. Heardle by Spotify
  • 8. World’s Hardest Game
  • 9. Akinator
  • 10. Helicopter Game
  • 11. Mars Tomorrow
  • 12. Snail Bob
  • 13. Squadd.io
  • 14. Wordle
  • 15. Pokemon Showdown
  • 16. Agar.io
  • 17. City Guesser
  • 18. Quick, Draw!
  • 19. Sunset Bike Racer
  • 20. Fallen London
  • 21. Treasure Arena
  • 22. Prodigy
  • 23. Townscaper
  • 24. Prince of Persia
  • 25. Coma
  • 26. Krunker
  • 27. Mole
  • 28. Tetris
  • 29. Scary Maze
  • 30. Pixel Starships
  • 31. GuessWhereYouAre.com

Best Browser Games You Must Play in 2025 

Now you will never be bored with these great picks right here.

1. War Brokers

For those who love first-person shooter games, War Brokers delivers an action-packed experience right in your browser. This voxel-based shooter offers crisp graphics, smooth performance, and a variety of missions to keep you hooked. From urban battles to desert warfare, every map offers something new. You can even hop into tanks, helicopters, or armored vehicles to dominate the field. Creating an account allows you to save weapon upgrades and track progress for future matches.

2. Skribbl

Skribbl is the ultimate online drawing and guessing game that lets you play with friends or strangers. Each round gives players a word to draw while others try to guess it before time runs out. You can even create private lobbies, add inside jokes, or set custom word lists for more fun. It’s simple, fast, and full of hilarious misinterpretations that make every match unpredictable and one of the best browser games you must play.

3. Slither.io

Slither.io reimagines the classic Snake game with a competitive multiplayer twist. The goal is to eat glowing dots, grow your snake, and survive longer than everyone else on the map. But there’s a catch, touch another snake, and it’s game over. Outwit opponents to make them crash into you, then scoop up their energy to grow even larger. Quick reactions and a bit of strategy are all you need to top the leaderboard.

4. Slow Roads

After a long day, Slow Roads feels like the perfect digital escape. This endless driving game lets you cruise through scenic landscapes that change with every play, from sunny valleys to foggy hills. There’s no timer, no competition, just smooth driving and calming vibes. You can pick your ride, whether a car, bike, or even a coach bus, and switch between different times of day and seasons. It’s more about relaxing and soaking in the view than racing to the finish line.

5. NeoPets

NeoPets takes you back to the internet’s golden age of virtual pets, where every creature had a story and every login felt like visiting a tiny world of your own. You start by adopting a Neopet and caring for it through feeding, playing, and joining fun events. Beyond pet care, there’s an entire fantasy world full of species, lands, and lore to uncover. The platform even has chatrooms and forums where you can trade, play, and connect with other players. It’s nostalgic, cozy, and still one of the most charming browser games out there.

6. RuneScape

RuneScape remains one of the most iconic browser MMOs ever created. Since its 2001 release, its world has evolved into a vast, living fantasy realm filled with cities, monsters, and endless quests. Players can fish, mine, craft, and battle, or simply explore its open world at their own pace. The level-up system rewards dedication, allowing you to grow stronger with each skill mastered. It’s not just a game; it’s one of the best browser games you must play.

7. Heardle by Spotify

If you love guessing songs, Heardle will instantly hook you. This music-based browser game challenges you to identify a track from just a short sound clip; the faster you guess, the better. You don’t even need a Spotify account to play, but the integration makes it easy to add songs you discover to your playlist. It’s fun solo, but even better with friends who love music battles. Simple, nostalgic, and oddly addictive, it’s the modern way to flex your music knowledge.

8. World’s Hardest Game

Don’t be fooled by its minimalist design, World’s Hardest Game is exactly what the name promises. Your goal is to guide a red block from start to finish while dodging moving obstacles. Sounds easy, until you realize every tiny mistake sends you back to the start. With 30 levels and infinite retries, it’s a brutal test of timing and patience. Each attempt makes victory that much sweeter, if you ever get there.

9. Akinator

Think of any person, object, or fictional character, and Akinator will try to guess it. Through a sequence of yes-or-no questions, this digital genie narrows down your thoughts with eerie accuracy. It’s simple, fascinating, and surprisingly good at reading your mind. Each session feels like a fun mental duel against A, and somehow, it almost always wins. Akinator proves that sometimes, the most entertaining games need nothing more than clever questions.

10. Helicopter Game

Before mobile games took over, the Helicopter Game ruled browser gaming. Using just your mouse, you guide a chopper through a tunnel filled with obstacles — click to go up, release to descend. It sounds easy, but quickly turns into a reflex test that’s as challenging as it is addicting. Your score depends on how far you can fly before crashing, with each round making you want to try just one more time. It’s pure arcade nostalgia in a single click.

11. Mars Tomorrow

Step into the future with Mars Tomorrow, a browser-based strategy game set in 2100. As Earth becomes unlivable, humanity looks to Mars for survival, and you’re in charge of making it happen. Build colonies, produce resources, and terraform the red planet into a habitable world. The real-time gameplay and atmospheric soundtrack make it both relaxing and deeply strategic, and one of the best browser games you must play.

12. Snail Bob

Snail Bob is an adorable puzzle adventure that follows Bob, a snail whose home has been destroyed. Your mission is to guide him safely through each level by solving clever puzzles and activating levers. The point-and-click gameplay is easy to pick up, while the increasing difficulty keeps things interesting. The game saves your progress automatically, so you can always return to continue Bob’s journey.

13. Squadd.io

If you enjoy top-down shooters, Squadd.io will keep you entertained for hours. It’s a fast-paced multiplayer brawler where you and your team must survive as long as possible while defeating enemies. Every victory earns you experience points, unlocking new characters and weapons. With its simple controls and quick matchmaking, it’s a great pick for short, intense gaming sessions.

14. Wordle

Wordle has become a daily ritual for puzzle fans around the world. The browser-based word game challenges you to guess a five-letter word in six tries. Each guess reveals color-coded hints: green for correct letters in the right spot, yellow for correct letters in the wrong spot, and grey for incorrect ones. Simple yet addictive, Wordle sharpens your vocabulary and logic skills one puzzle at a time.

15. Pokemon Showdown

Jump straight into competitive Pokémon battles without the wait in Pokémon Showdown. This browser-based simulator lets you build a team and challenge players around the world instantly. Strategy is everything; the moves you pick and how you counter your opponent decide your victory. Whether you’re a casual fan or a competitive trainer, the thrill of testing your skills in real-time battles never fades. You can even download it on PC for a smoother experience.

16. Agar.io

Agar.io takes simplicity and turns it into an obsession. You begin as a small cell, absorbing tiny dots to grow bigger while dodging larger players who want to eat you. As you gain size, your speed drops, making every move a balance between risk and reward. The ability to split into smaller cells adds another layer of strategy. It’s fast, ruthless, and surprisingly addictive, perfect for short but intense gaming bursts, making it one of the best browser games you must play.

17. City Guesser

Explore the world through your browser with City Guesser, a geography guessing game powered by real street footage. Watch a random city video and use clues like signs, architecture, and vehicles to pinpoint its location on the map. Your accuracy and speed determine your score. The multiplayer mode makes it even more exciting, letting you challenge friends on Discord or join global lobbies. It’s a game that blends curiosity, learning, and travel, all from your chair.

18. Quick, Draw!

Ever wondered how well an AI can understand your doodles? Quick, Draw! challenges you to sketch random objects in under 20 seconds while Google’s AI guesses what you’ve drawn. The more accurately and quickly you draw, the higher your chances of moving forward. It’s part art, part chaos, and completely hilarious, especially when your cat looks like a jellybean.

19. Sunset Bike Racer

Experience high-octane racing against a stunning sunset backdrop in Sunset Bike Racer. Master tricky tracks filled with jumps, flips, and stunts as you race against the clock. Each motorcycle comes with its own handling and performance traits, so pick wisely based on your style. The game’s smooth physics and vibrant visuals make every level exciting. Whether you’re aiming for perfect landings or record-breaking times, the rush never stops.

20. Fallen London

Lose yourself in the eerie charm of Fallen London, a dark, text-based adventure with endless stories to uncover. You begin by creating a character and exploring an underground version of Victorian London. Choices matter here, as every decision can lead to fame, fortune, or ruin. With its branching narratives and an economy built around “echoes,” the game rewards clever thinking and curiosity. Constant updates keep this gothic world alive and ever-evolving.

21. Treasure Arena

Step into a retro-style pixel dungeon where gold is everything in Treasure Arena. Compete against other players as you battle monsters, dodge traps, and collect as much treasure as possible before the timer runs out. Death isn’t the end; you’ll respawn endlessly until time expires. When it’s over, the richest player wins. Fast, chaotic, and full of surprises, it’s a perfect blend of nostalgia and competitive fun, making it one of the best browser games you must play.

22. Prodigy

Prodigy combines math learning with a fantasy MMORPG twist, making education surprisingly fun. With over 50 million players worldwide, this adventure lets you explore magical worlds, battle monsters, and solve math questions to progress. Designed mainly for younger players, it’s both educational and engaging. Each correct answer strengthens your character, turning study time into a rewarding quest.

23. Townscaper

Townscaper is all about slow creativity, no rules, no time limits, just imagination. You start by dropping colorful blocks on a grid, and like magic, the game automatically transforms them into houses, towers, bridges, or cozy courtyards. There are no scores or levels, it’s just you designing your dream seaside town. The minimal interface and calming sound design make it one of the most relaxing browser games to unwind with after a long day.

24. Prince of Persia

A true classic reborn in 2D form, Prince of Persia brings Ubisoft’s legendary action-platformer right into your browser. You play as the young prince navigating through dungeons filled with traps, guards, and puzzles, all to rescue the princess from the villain Jaffar. Each level demands precision jumps, quick reflexes, and a bit of patience. Its smooth animations and intricate level design still hold up beautifully, proving to be one of the best browser games you must play.

25. Coma

Coma is a poetic adventure wrapped in a dreamlike world. You play as Pete, a small creature journeying through a surreal landscape filled with floating trees, hidden passages, and hauntingly beautiful piano music. Along the way, you’ll meet strange characters and even free a bird who becomes your companion. There’s no save option, so you must finish the game in one sitting, which only adds to its fleeting, almost meditative experience.

26. Krunker

Imagine Counter-Strike and Minecraft had a baby, that’s Krunker. This fast-paced FPS runs right in your browser, no downloads or sign-ins required. Its 8-bit visuals give it a blocky charm, while the gameplay feels as sharp and competitive as any shooter. You can join public matches or create private lobbies for friends. With game modes like Zombies, Raids, and Custom Maps, plus a Battle Pass system for new skins and items, Krunker delivers endless replayability.

27. Mole

Don’t let its simplicity fool you, Mole is one tough game. You control a tiny mole using just the spacebar, guiding it down a narrow cave while dodging obstacles and walls. Each of its 18 levels introduces new challenges that test timing and precision. The trick is to plan every jump carefully while using the small ledges to catch your breath. It’s minimalist, but deeply satisfying when you finally master the rhythm, making it one of the best browser games you must play.

28. Tetris

The king of puzzle games needs no introduction. Tetris in your browser retains its classic charm but adds vibrant neon colors and smooth controls. The goal is the same: arrange the falling blocks to form complete lines and clear the screen. As the pace speeds up, your quick thinking and hand-eye coordination are put to the test. Customize controls, chase high scores, and lose track of time just like the good old days.

29. Scary Maze

At first glance, Scary Maze seems like a harmless concentration game, guiding a small dot through a narrow maze using steady hands. But then, without warning, the calm is shattered by a sudden jump scare and scream. It’s become infamous online as the ultimate prank game to trick your friends. Just remember, it’s all fun and games until you’re the one holding the mouse!

30. Pixel Starships

Set in a vibrant 8-bit universe, Pixel Starships brings a nostalgic yet complex MMORPG experience straight to your browser. You design and build your own starship, manage its crew, balance power systems, and engage in tactical battles with players across the galaxy. Every decision matters, from which weapons to equip to how your team reacts under pressure in real-time combat. With alien races, deep customization, and strategic gameplay. It’s a perfect mix of creativity and competition that keeps you hooked for hours.

31. GuessWhereYouAre.com

If you’ve ever dreamed of traveling the world from your desk, GuessWhereYouAre.com makes it possible and competitive. You’re dropped into random locations via street view, and your task is to guess where you are on the map. The closer your guess, the higher your score. What makes it addictive is the live multiplayer mode, where you face off against players worldwide, climb ELO rankings, and test your geography instincts in real time. It’s the perfect blend of learning and fun; every wrong guess just makes you want to try again.

Now you will no longer have a difficult time figuring out the best browser games you must play in 2025 after following this guide. For more helpful tips and tricks, stay tuned, and feel free to share your suggestions in the comments below.

There’s no timer, no competition, just smooth driving and calming vibes. You can pick your ride, whether a car, bike, or even a coach bus, and switch between different times of day and seasons. It’s more about relaxing and soaking in the view than racing to the finish line.

5. NeoPets

NeoPets takes you back to the internet’s golden age of virtual pets, where every creature had a story and every login felt like visiting a tiny world of your own. You start by adopting a Neopet and caring for it through feeding, playing, and joining fun events. Beyond pet care, there’s an entire fantasy world full of species, lands, and lore to uncover. The platform even has chatrooms and forums where you can trade, play, and connect with other players. It’s nostalgic, cozy, and still one of the most charming browser games out there.

6. RuneScape

RuneScape remains one of the most iconic browser MMOs ever created. Since its 2001 release, its world has evolved into a vast, living fantasy realm filled with cities, monsters, and endless quests. Players can fish, mine, craft, and battle, or simply explore its open world at their own pace. The level-up system rewards dedication, allowing you to grow stronger with each skill mastered. It’s not just a game; it’s one of the best browser games you must play.

7. Heardle by Spotify

If you love guessing songs, Heardle will instantly hook you. This music-based browser game challenges you to identify a track from just a short sound clip; the faster you guess, the better. You don’t even need a Spotify account to play, but the integration makes it easy to add songs you discover to your playlist. It’s fun solo, but even better with friends who love music battles. Simple, nostalgic, and oddly addictive, it’s the modern way to flex your music knowledge.

8. World’s Hardest Game

Don’t be fooled by its minimalist design, World’s Hardest Game is exactly what the name promises. Your goal is to guide a red block from start to finish while dodging moving obstacles. Sounds easy, until you realize every tiny mistake sends you back to the start. With 30 levels and infinite retries, it’s a brutal test of timing and patience. Each attempt makes victory that much sweeter, if you ever get there.

9. Akinator

Think of any person, object, or fictional character, and Akinator will try to guess it. Through a sequence of yes-or-no questions, this digital genie narrows down your thoughts with eerie accuracy. It’s simple, fascinating, and surprisingly good at reading your mind. Each session feels like a fun mental duel against A, and somehow, it almost always wins. Akinator proves that sometimes, the most entertaining games need nothing more than clever questions.

10. Helicopter Game

Before mobile games took over, the Helicopter Game ruled browser gaming. Using just your mouse, you guide a chopper through a tunnel filled with obstacles — click to go up, release to descend. It sounds easy, but quickly turns into a reflex test that’s as challenging as it is addicting. Your score depends on how far you can fly before crashing, with each round making you want to try just one more time. It’s pure arcade nostalgia in a single click.

11. Mars Tomorrow

Step into the future with Mars Tomorrow, a browser-based strategy game set in 2100. As Earth becomes unlivable, humanity looks to Mars for survival, and you’re in charge of making it happen. Build colonies, produce resources, and terraform the red planet into a habitable world. The real-time gameplay and atmospheric soundtrack make it both relaxing and deeply strategic, and one of the best browser games you must play.

12. Snail Bob

Snail Bob is an adorable puzzle adventure that follows Bob, a snail whose home has been destroyed. Your mission is to guide him safely through each level by solving clever puzzles and activating levers. The point-and-click gameplay is easy to pick up, while the increasing difficulty keeps things interesting. The game saves your progress automatically, so you can always return to continue Bob’s journey.

13. Squadd.io

If you enjoy top-down shooters, Squadd.io will keep you entertained for hours. It’s a fast-paced multiplayer brawler where you and your team must survive as long as possible while defeating enemies. Every victory earns you experience points, unlocking new characters and weapons. With its simple controls and quick matchmaking, it’s a great pick for short, intense gaming sessions.

14. Wordle

Wordle has become a daily ritual for puzzle fans around the world. The browser-based word game challenges you to guess a five-letter word in six tries. Each guess reveals color-coded hints: green for correct letters in the right spot, yellow for correct letters in the wrong spot, and grey for incorrect ones. Simple yet addictive, Wordle sharpens your vocabulary and logic skills one puzzle at a time.

15. Pokemon Showdown

Jump straight into competitive Pokémon battles without the wait in Pokémon Showdown. This browser-based simulator lets you build a team and challenge players around the world instantly. Strategy is everything; the moves you pick and how you counter your opponent decide your victory. Whether you’re a casual fan or a competitive trainer, the thrill of testing your skills in real-time battles never fades. You can even download it on PC for a smoother experience.

16. Agar.io

Agar.io takes simplicity and turns it into an obsession. You begin as a small cell, absorbing tiny dots to grow bigger while dodging larger players who want to eat you. As you gain size, your speed drops, making every move a balance between risk and reward. The ability to split into smaller cells adds another layer of strategy. It’s fast, ruthless, and surprisingly addictive, perfect for short but intense gaming bursts, making it one of the best browser games you must play.

17. City Guesser

Explore the world through your browser with City Guesser, a geography guessing game powered by real street footage. Watch a random city video and use clues like signs, architecture, and vehicles to pinpoint its location on the map. Your accuracy and speed determine your score. The multiplayer mode makes it even more exciting, letting you challenge friends on Discord or join global lobbies. It’s a game that blends curiosity, learning, and travel, all from your chair.

18. Quick, Draw!

Ever wondered how well an AI can understand your doodles? Quick, Draw! challenges you to sketch random objects in under 20 seconds while Google’s AI guesses what you’ve drawn. The more accurately and quickly you draw, the higher your chances of moving forward. It’s part art, part chaos, and completely hilarious, especially when your cat looks like a jellybean.

19. Sunset Bike Racer

Experience high-octane racing against a stunning sunset backdrop in Sunset Bike Racer. Master tricky tracks filled with jumps, flips, and stunts as you race against the clock. Each motorcycle comes with its own handling and performance traits, so pick wisely based on your style. The game’s smooth physics and vibrant visuals make every level exciting. Whether you’re aiming for perfect landings or record-breaking times, the rush never stops.

20. Fallen London

Lose yourself in the eerie charm of Fallen London, a dark, text-based adventure with endless stories to uncover. You begin by creating a character and exploring an underground version of Victorian London. Choices matter here, as every decision can lead to fame, fortune, or ruin. With its branching narratives and an economy built around “echoes,” the game rewards clever thinking and curiosity. Constant updates keep this gothic world alive and ever-evolving.

21. Treasure Arena

Step into a retro-style pixel dungeon where gold is everything in Treasure Arena. Compete against other players as you battle monsters, dodge traps, and collect as much treasure as possible before the timer runs out. Death isn’t the end; you’ll respawn endlessly until time expires. When it’s over, the richest player wins. Fast, chaotic, and full of surprises, it’s a perfect blend of nostalgia and competitive fun, making it one of the best browser games you must play.

22. Prodigy

Prodigy combines math learning with a fantasy MMORPG twist, making education surprisingly fun. With over 50 million players worldwide, this adventure lets you explore magical worlds, battle monsters, and solve math questions to progress. Designed mainly for younger players, it’s both educational and engaging. Each correct answer strengthens your character, turning study time into a rewarding quest.

23. Townscaper

Townscaper is all about slow creativity, no rules, no time limits, just imagination. You start by dropping colorful blocks on a grid, and like magic, the game automatically transforms them into houses, towers, bridges, or cozy courtyards. There are no scores or levels, it’s just you designing your dream seaside town. The minimal interface and calming sound design make it one of the most relaxing browser games to unwind with after a long day.

24. Prince of Persia

A true classic reborn in 2D form, Prince of Persia brings Ubisoft’s legendary action-platformer right into your browser. You play as the young prince navigating through dungeons filled with traps, guards, and puzzles, all to rescue the princess from the villain Jaffar. Each level demands precision jumps, quick reflexes, and a bit of patience. Its smooth animations and intricate level design still hold up beautifully, proving to be one of the best browser games you must play.

25. Coma

Coma is a poetic adventure wrapped in a dreamlike world. You play as Pete, a small creature journeying through a surreal landscape filled with floating trees, hidden passages, and hauntingly beautiful piano music. Along the way, you’ll meet strange characters and even free a bird who becomes your companion. There’s no save option, so you must finish the game in one sitting, which only adds to its fleeting, almost meditative experience.

26. Krunker

Imagine Counter-Strike and Minecraft had a baby, that’s Krunker. This fast-paced FPS runs right in your browser, no downloads or sign-ins required. Its 8-bit visuals give it a blocky charm, while the gameplay feels as sharp and competitive as any shooter. You can join public matches or create private lobbies for friends. With game modes like Zombies, Raids, and Custom Maps, plus a Battle Pass system for new skins and items, Krunker delivers endless replayability.

27. Mole

Don’t let its simplicity fool you, Mole is one tough game. You control a tiny mole using just the spacebar, guiding it down a narrow cave while dodging obstacles and walls. Each of its 18 levels introduces new challenges that test timing and precision. The trick is to plan every jump carefully while using the small ledges to catch your breath. It’s minimalist, but deeply satisfying when you finally master the rhythm, making it one of the best browser games you must play.

28. Tetris

The king of puzzle games needs no introduction. Tetris in your browser retains its classic charm but adds vibrant neon colors and smooth controls. The goal is the same: arrange the falling blocks to form complete lines and clear the screen. As the pace speeds up, your quick thinking and hand-eye coordination are put to the test. Customize controls, chase high scores, and lose track of time just like the good old days.

29. Scary Maze

At first glance, Scary Maze seems like a harmless concentration game, guiding a small dot through a narrow maze using steady hands. But then, without warning, the calm is shattered by a sudden jump scare and scream. It’s become infamous online as the ultimate prank game to trick your friends. Just remember, it’s all fun and games until you’re the one holding the mouse!

30. Pixel Starships

Set in a vibrant 8-bit universe, Pixel Starships brings a nostalgic yet complex MMORPG experience straight to your browser. You design and build your own starship, manage its crew, balance power systems, and engage in tactical battles with players across the galaxy. Every decision matters, from which weapons to equip to how your team reacts under pressure in real-time combat. With alien races, deep customization, and strategic gameplay. It’s a perfect mix of creativity and competition that keeps you hooked for hours.

31. GuessWhereYouAre.com

If you’ve ever dreamed of traveling the world from your desk, GuessWhereYouAre.com makes it possible and competitive. You’re dropped into random locations via street view, and your task is to guess where you are on the map. The closer your guess, the higher your score. What makes it addictive is the live multiplayer mode, where you face off against players worldwide, climb ELO rankings, and test your geography instincts in real time. It’s the perfect blend of learning and fun; every wrong guess just makes you want to try again.

Best Browser Games to Play in 2026 

Now you will never be bored with these great picks right here.

1. War Brokers

For those who love first-person shooter games, War Brokers delivers an action-packed experience right in your browser. This voxel-based shooter offers crisp graphics, smooth performance, and a variety of missions to keep you hooked. From urban battles to desert warfare, every map offers something new. You can even hop into tanks, helicopters, or armored vehicles to dominate the field. Creating an account allows you to save weapon upgrades and track progress for future matches.

2. Skribbl

Skribbl is the ultimate online drawing and guessing game that lets you play with friends or strangers. Each round gives players a word to draw while others try to guess it before time runs out. You can even create private lobbies, add inside jokes, or set custom word lists for more fun. It’s simple, fast, and full of hilarious misinterpretations that make every match unpredictable and one of the best browser games to play.

3. Slither.io

Slither.io reimagines the classic Snake game with a competitive multiplayer twist. The goal is to eat glowing dots, grow your snake, and survive longer than everyone else on the map. But there’s a catch: touch another snake, and it’s game over. Outwit opponents to make them crash into you, then scoop up their energy to grow even larger. Quick reactions and a bit of strategy are all you need to top the leaderboard.

4. Slow Roads

After a long day, Slow Roads feels like the perfect digital escape. This endless driving game lets you cruise through scenic landscapes that change with every play, from sunny valleys to foggy hills. There’s no timer, no competition, just smooth driving and calming vibes. You can pick your ride, whether a car, bike, or even a coach bus, and switch between different times of day and seasons. It’s more about relaxing and soaking in the view than racing to the finish line.

5. NeoPets

NeoPets takes you back to the internet’s golden age of virtual pets, where every creature had a story and every login felt like visiting a tiny world of your own. You start by adopting a Neopet and caring for it through feeding, playing, and joining fun events. Beyond pet care, there’s an entire fantasy world full of species, lands, and lore to uncover. The platform even has chatrooms and forums where you can trade, play, and connect with other players. It’s nostalgic, cozy, and still one of the most charming browser games out there.

6. RuneScape

RuneScape remains one of the most iconic browser MMOs ever created. Since its 2001 release, its world has evolved into a vast, living fantasy realm filled with cities, monsters, and endless quests. Players can fish, mine, craft, and battle, or simply explore its open world at their own pace. The level-up system rewards dedication, allowing you to grow stronger with each skill mastered. It’s not just a game; it’s one of the best browser games to play.

7. Heardle by Spotify

If you love guessing songs, Heardle will instantly hook you. This music-based browser game challenges you to identify a track from just a short sound clip; the faster you guess, the better. You don’t even need a Spotify account to play, but the integration makes it easy to add songs you discover to your playlist. It’s fun solo, but even better with friends who love music battles.
